| `Bluetooth.deviceIcon(device)`    | Nerd Font glyph for the device icon key.                                                                                                                                                  |
| `Bluetooth.iconForState()`        | Adapter glyph based on availability, block, transition, discovery, connection, and power.                                                                                                 |
| `Bluetooth.iconKeyForState()`     | Adapter key: `bluetooth-off`, `bluetooth-blocked`, `bluetooth-discovering`, `bluetooth-connected`, `bluetooth`.                                                                           |

### Serialization

| How to call                      | What does it do                                                                                          |
| -------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Bluetooth.deviceInfo(device)`   | Returns a plain JSON-safe object for one device. Returns `{}` for null.                                  |
| `Bluetooth.adapterInfo(adapter)` | Returns a plain JSON-safe object for one adapter including its connected devices. Returns `{}` for null. |
| `Bluetooth.statusInfo()`         | Returns the complete service status object used by IPC `getStatus`.                                      |

### Signals

| Signal                        | When it fires                                                                 |
| ----------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `adapterAdded(var adapter)`   | A BlueZ adapter object was inserted.                                          |
| `adapterRemoved(var adapter)` | A BlueZ adapter object was removed.                                           |
| `deviceAdded(var device)`     | A BlueZ device object was inserted.                                           |
| `deviceRemoved(var device)`   | A BlueZ device object was removed.                                            |
| `stateChangedExternally()`    | Default adapter, adapter list, or device list changed underneath the service. |
| `adapterListUpdated()`        | Adapter model changed or default adapter changed.                             |
| `deviceListUpdated()`         | Device model changed.                                                         |

For example:

```qml
Connections {
    target: Bluetooth

    function onDeviceAdded(device) {
        console.log(
            "added:",
            Bluetooth.displayName(device)
        )
    }

    function onDeviceListUpdated() {
        console.log(
            "devices:",
            Bluetooth.deviceCount
        )
    }
}
```

### Typical component usage

A panel toggle only needs the headline properties:

```qml
readonly property bool available:
    Bluetooth.isAvailable

readonly property bool enabled:
    Bluetooth.isEnabled

readonly property string icon:
    Bluetooth.icon

readonly property string activeName:
    Bluetooth.activeDeviceName
```

A device row only needs lookup plus one action:

```qml
readonly property var device:
    Bluetooth.findDevice(
        "AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF"
    )

readonly property string name:
    Bluetooth.displayName(
        device
    )

readonly property bool connected:
    device
        ? device.connected
        : false
```

That is the intended everyday usage.

Components normally should not need to touch raw `Quickshell.Bluetooth` models directly.

***

# 3. IPC API

IPC target:

```text
n0ctos-bluetooth
```

## Core adapter and discovery

| How to call                        | What does it do                            |
| ---------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| `getStatus`                        | Returns `statusInfo()` as a JSON string.   |
| `getState`                         | Returns `stateName`.                       |
| `getIcon`                          | Returns the adapter icon glyph.            |
| `getAdapter`                       | Returns `adapterName`.                     |
| `getAdapterId`                     | Returns `adapterId`.                       |
| `getEnabled`                       | Returns `"true"` or `"false"`.             |
| `setEnabled <true\|false>`         | Sets adapter power.                        |
| `toggle`                           | Flips the current power state.             |
| `getDiscovering`                   | Returns `"true"` or `"false"`.             |
| `startDiscovery`                   | Starts discovery on every enabled adapter. |
| `stopDiscovery`                    | Stops discovery on every adapter.          |
| `getDiscoverable`                  | Returns `"true"` or `"false"`.             |
| `setDiscoverable <true\|false>`    | Sets discoverable mode.                    |
| `setDiscoverableTimeout <seconds>` | Sets discoverable timeout.                 |
| `getPairable`                      | Returns `"true"` or `"false"`.             |
| `setPairable <true\|false>`        | Sets pairable mode.                        |
| `setPairableTimeout <seconds>`     | Sets pairable timeout.                     |

| Example                                                   | Result                                                        |
| --------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `qs ipc call n0ctos-bluetooth getStatus`                  | JSON status object                                            |
| `qs ipc call n0ctos-bluetooth getState`                   | state string, e.g. `"Enabled"` (`"Disabled"` with no adapter) |
| `qs ipc call n0ctos-bluetooth getIcon`                    | adapter Nerd Font glyph                                       |
| `qs ipc call n0ctos-bluetooth getAdapter`                 | adapter name, or `""`                                         |
| `qs ipc call n0ctos-bluetooth getAdapterId`               | `"hci0"`, or `""`                                             |
| `qs ipc call n0ctos-bluetooth getEnabled`                 | `"true"` or `"false"`                                         |
| `qs ipc call n0ctos-bluetooth setEnabled true`            | adapter powers on                                             |
| `qs ipc call n0ctos-bluetooth toggle`                     | power state flips                                             |
| `qs ipc call n0ctos-bluetooth getDiscovering`             | `"true"` or `"false"`                                         |
| `qs ipc call n0ctos-bluetooth startDiscovery`             | discovery starts on enabled adapters                          |
| `qs ipc call n0ctos-bluetooth stopDiscovery`              | discovery stops                                               |
| `qs ipc call n0ctos-bluetooth getDiscoverable`            | `"true"` or `"false"`                                         |
| `qs ipc call n0ctos-bluetooth setDiscoverable true`       | adapter becomes discoverable                                  |
| `qs ipc call n0ctos-bluetooth setDiscoverableTimeout 120` | timeout becomes 120 s                                         |
| `qs ipc call n0ctos-bluetooth getPairable`                | `"true"` or `"false"`                                         |
| `qs ipc call n0ctos-bluetooth setPairable true`           | adapter becomes pairable                                      |
| `qs ipc call n0ctos-bluetooth setPairableTimeout 0`       | timeout becomes 0 (no timeout)                                |

Boolean arguments use QML bools over IPC:

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-bluetooth setEnabled true
```

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-bluetooth setEnabled false
```

Timeouts are integers in seconds:

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-bluetooth setDiscoverableTimeout 120
```

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-bluetooth setPairableTimeout 0
```

Toggle needs no argument:

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-bluetooth toggle
```

## Other operations

| How to call                              | What does it do                                                         |
| ---------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `getDevices`                             | Returns every tracked device as a JSON array of `deviceInfo()` objects. |
| `getConnectedDevices`                    | Returns connected devices as a JSON array.                              |
| `getPairedDevices`                       | Returns paired devices as a JSON array.                                 |
| `connect <address>`                      | Connects one device by MAC address.                                     |
| `disconnect <address>`                   | Disconnects one device by MAC address.                                  |
| `pair <address>`                         | Pairs one device by MAC address.                                        |
| `cancelPair <address>`                   | Cancels an in-progress pairing.                                         |
| `forget <address>`                       | Forgets one device by MAC address.                                      |
| `setTrusted <address> <true\|false>`     | Sets the trusted flag.                                                  |
| `setBlocked <address> <true\|false>`     | Sets the blocked flag.                                                  |
| `setWakeAllowed <address> <true\|false>` | Sets wake-allowed.                                                      |
| `setName <address> <name>`               | Sets the device alias.                                                  |

| Example                                                              | Result                               |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| `qs ipc call n0ctos-bluetooth getDevices`                            | JSON array of `deviceInfo()` objects |
| `qs ipc call n0ctos-bluetooth getConnectedDevices`                   | JSON array of connected devices      |
| `qs ipc call n0ctos-bluetooth getPairedDevices`                      | JSON array of paired devices         |
| `qs ipc call n0ctos-bluetooth connect AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF`             | device starts connecting             |
| `qs ipc call n0ctos-bluetooth disconnect AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF`          | device disconnects                   |
| `qs ipc call n0ctos-bluetooth pair AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF`                | pairing starts                       |
| `qs ipc call n0ctos-bluetooth cancelPair AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF`          | in-progress pairing cancelled        |
| `qs ipc call n0ctos-bluetooth forget AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF`              | device removed                       |
| `qs ipc call n0ctos-bluetooth setTrusted AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF true`     | device becomes trusted               |
| `qs ipc call n0ctos-bluetooth setBlocked AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF false`    | device becomes unblocked             |
| `qs ipc call n0ctos-bluetooth setWakeAllowed AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF true` | device may wake the system           |
| `qs ipc call n0ctos-bluetooth setName AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF Headphones`  | alias becomes `Headphones`           |

Device addresses are case-insensitive:

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-bluetooth connect AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF
```

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-bluetooth disconnect aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff
```

Policy flags use bools:

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-bluetooth setTrusted \
    AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF \
    true
```

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-bluetooth setBlocked \
    AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF \
    false
```

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-bluetooth setWakeAllowed \
    AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF \
    true
```

Rename:

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-bluetooth setName \
    AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF \
    Headphones
```

List operations return JSON strings. Pipe through `jq` when available:

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-bluetooth getDevices | jq .
```

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-bluetooth getConnectedDevices | jq .
```

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-bluetooth getStatus | jq .
```

***

# 4. Features / limitations

## Features

### Multi-adapter tracking

The service exposes both the raw adapter model and convenient shortcuts:

```text
adapters
adapterList
adapterCount
defaultAdapter
```

Discovery operates across adapters:

```text
startDiscovery
    ↓
every enabled adapter
    discovering = true
```

```text
stopDiscovery
    ↓
every adapter
    discovering = false
```

This handles machines with more than one Bluetooth controller.

### Filtered device collections

The global device model is filtered into ready-to-bind lists:

```text
devices
    ├── connectedDevices
    ├── pairedDevices
    ├── bondedDevices
    ├── batteryDevices
    └── connectedBatteryDevices
```

Each collection exposes three forms:

```text
connectedDevices
connectedDeviceList
connectedDeviceCount
```

A component can bind to the count for a pill, the list for a menu, or the model for a view.

### Active device

The service resolves one headline device:

```text
first device.connected
    ↓
activeDevice
```

with derived properties:

```text
activeDeviceName
activeDeviceAddress
isDeviceConnected
hasDeviceBattery
activeDeviceBattery
activeDeviceBatteryRounded
activeDeviceBatteryText
```

A status bar therefore needs only:

```qml
Bluetooth.activeDeviceName
```

### Battery normalization

Quickshell reports battery as:

```text
0.0 -> 1.0
```

The service converts it to the public range:

```text
0 -> 100
```

For example:

```qml
Bluetooth.batteryPercent(
    device
)
```

returns a clamped percent, or `0` when battery is unavailable or non-finite.

`deviceInfo()` therefore contains:

```json
{
    "isBatteryAvailable": true,
    "battery": 82.0,
    "batteryRounded": 82,
    "batteryText": "82%"
}
```

and `null` battery fields when no battery is available.

### Per-device icons

Device icons are derived from both BlueZ icon text and the display name:

```qml
Bluetooth.deviceIconKey(
    device
)
```

The supported keys are:

```text
headphones
speaker
keyboard
mouse
gamepad
phone
tablet
laptop
printer
camera
television
bluetooth
```

For example, any source text containing:

```text
headset
headphone
earbud
```

maps to:

```text
headphones
```

`deviceIcon()` then maps each key to a Nerd Font glyph.

### Adapter icons

The headline icon reflects priority state:

```text
no adapter -> off
blocked -> off
disabling -> off
enabling -> on
discovering -> on
connected device -> connected
enabled -> on
otherwise -> off
```

Both forms are available:

```qml
Bluetooth.icon
```

```qml
Bluetooth.iconKey
```

### JSON serialization

Three serializers produce IPC- and UI-safe data:

```text
deviceInfo(device)
adapterInfo(adapter)
statusInfo()
```

A device object looks like:

```json
{
    "name": "WH-1000XM5",
    "deviceName": "WH-1000XM5",
    "address": "AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF",
    "dbusPath": "/org/bluez/hci0/dev_AA_BB_CC_DD_EE_FF",
    "adapter": "hci0",
    "adapterName": "MyMachine",
    "state": "Connected",
    "isConnected": true,
    "isConnecting": false,
    "isDisconnecting": false,
    "isPaired": true,
    "isBonded": true,
    "isPairing": false,
    "isTrusted": true,
    "isBlocked": false,
    "isWakeAllowed": true,
    "isBatteryAvailable": true,
    "battery": 82.0,
    "batteryRounded": 82,
    "batteryText": "82%",
    "icon": "󰋋",
    "iconKey": "headphones"
}
```

An adapter object looks like:

```json
{
    "name": "MyMachine",
    "adapterId": "hci0",
    "dbusPath": "/org/bluez/hci0",
    "state": "Enabled",
    "isEnabled": true,
    "isDiscoverable": false,
    "isDiscovering": false,
    "isPairable": true,
    "discoverableTimeout": 0,
    "pairableTimeout": 0,
    "deviceCount": 3,
    "connectedDeviceCount": 1,
    "connectedDevices": []
}
```

A status object looks like:

```json
{
    "isAvailable": true,
    "isEnabled": true,
    "isPowered": true,
    "isBlocked": false,
    "isEnabling": false,
    "isDisabling": false,
    "state": "Enabled",
    "adapter": "MyMachine",
    "adapterId": "hci0",
    "isDiscoverable": false,
    "isDiscovering": false,
    "isPairable": true,
    "discoverableTimeout": 0,
    "pairableTimeout": 0,
    "adapterCount": 1,
    "deviceCount": 3,
    "connectedDeviceCount": 1,
    "pairedDeviceCount": 2,
    "bondedDeviceCount": 2,
    "batteryDeviceCount": 1,
    "activeDevice": "WH-1000XM5",
    "activeDeviceAddress": "AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF",
    "hasDeviceBattery": true,
    "activeDeviceBattery": 82,
    "icon": "󰂱",
    "iconKey": "bluetooth-connected"
}
```

### Reactive signals

Adapter and device insertions propagate immediately:

```text
BlueZ change
    │
    ▼
Quickshell model signal
    │
    ▼
Bluetooth signal
    │
    ▼
component binding reevaluates
```

Components can listen for:

```text
adapterAdded
adapterRemoved
deviceAdded
deviceRemoved
stateChangedExternally
adapterListUpdated
deviceListUpdated
```

### Guarded control

Control functions fail safely:

```text
setEnabled
setDiscoverable
setPairable
    ↓
no default adapter -> return
```

```text
connectDevice
    ↓
unknown address -> return
blocked device -> return
```

```text
pairDevice
    ↓
unknown -> return
already paired -> return
already pairing -> return
```

```text
cancelPairDevice
    ↓
not pairing -> return
```

This prevents common BlueZ errors from throwing in QML.

### Case-insensitive lookup

Both lookup helpers normalize case:

```qml
Bluetooth.findDevice(
    "aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff"
)
```

matches:

```text
AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF
```

and:

```qml
Bluetooth.findDeviceByName(
    "wh-1000xm5"
)
```

matches:

```text
WH-1000XM5
```

### No polling

The service does not repeatedly scan BlueZ.

It relies on Quickshell's reactive adapter/device models and `Connections` handlers.

### No Config dependency

The service does not use `Config`.

There is no:

```text
bluetooth profile
bluetooth persistence
homeConfig section
```

Bluetooth state lives in BlueZ, not in N0ctOS configuration files.

***

## Limitations

### Requires a Bluetooth adapter

Without hardware or BlueZ:

```text
adapterCount = 0
defaultAdapter = null
isAvailable = false
stateName = "Disabled"
icon = off
activeDevice = null
```

Control calls become no-ops.

Check `isAvailable` before showing controls that assume hardware exists.

### Default-adapter writes

Power, discoverable, and pairable controls target:

```text
defaultAdapter
```

only.

For example:

```qml
Bluetooth.setEnabled(
    true
)
```

does not power every adapter individually.

Discovery is the exception: it iterates `adapterList`.

### Discovery only starts on enabled adapters

`startDiscovery()` skips adapters where:

```text
enabled = false
```

A disabled adapter therefore stays non-discovering even after a global start request.

### Blocked devices cannot connect

`connectDevice()` returns early when:

```text
device.blocked = true
```

Unblock the device first:

```qml
Bluetooth.setDeviceBlocked(
    address,
    false
)
```

then connect.

### Pairing guards are silent

`pairDevice()` ignores:

```text
unknown address
already paired
already pairing
```

and `cancelPairDevice()` ignores devices that are not pairing.

There is no returned error. Inspect device state when pairing behavior matters:

```qml
Bluetooth.isDeviceConnecting(
    device
)
```

```qml
Bluetooth.deviceStateName(
    device
)
```

### Active device is first-connected only

`activeDevice` is:

```text
the first device with connected = true
```

It is not a user-selected favorite, most-recent device, or audio-routing choice.

With multiple connected devices, only the first is surfaced as active.

### Display name is a fallback chain

`displayName()` uses:

```text
device.name trimmed
    ↓
device.deviceName
    ↓
""
```

An empty or whitespace-only alias therefore falls through to `deviceName`.

`findDeviceByName()` matches against that resolved display name, not the raw alias alone.

### Battery requires availability

`batteryPercent()` returns `0` unless:

```text
device.batteryAvailable = true
```

and the value is finite.

`deviceInfo()` uses `null` for `battery` and `batteryRounded` when unavailable, so UI code must handle:

```json
{
    "battery": null
}
```

### Serialized objects are snapshots

`deviceInfo()`, `adapterInfo()`, and `statusInfo()` return plain cloned data.

For example:

```qml
Bluetooth.deviceInfo(
    device
).isConnected
```

does not update when the device disconnects.

Bind to live properties such as:

```qml
device.connected
```

or:

```qml
Bluetooth.connectedDeviceCount
```

for reactive UI.

### No auto-reconnect or agent handling

The service does not implement:

```text
auto-reconnect policy
pairing-agent prompts
PIN handling
audio-profile switching
```

Those remain BlueZ / desktop responsibilities.

***

# 5. Example use cases

## 5.1 A panel toggle

A status pill only needs power, icon, and availability:

```qml
import QtQuick
import Quickshell

import qs.services

Item {
    readonly property bool available:
        Bluetooth.isAvailable

    readonly property bool enabled:
        Bluetooth.isEnabled

    readonly property string icon:
        Bluetooth.icon

    readonly property string label:
        !available
            ? "No Bluetooth"
            : enabled
                ? Bluetooth.activeDeviceName !== ""
                    ? Bluetooth.activeDeviceName
                    : "On"
                : "Off"
}
```

Toggle on click:

```qml
MouseArea {
    anchors.fill:
        parent

    enabled:
        Bluetooth.isAvailable

    onClicked:
        Bluetooth.setEnabled(
            !Bluetooth.isEnabled
        )
}
```

The icon updates automatically through:

```text
isAvailable
isBlocked
isEnabling / isDisabling
isDiscovering
connectedDeviceCount
isEnabled
```

***

## 5.2 A connected-device list

Bind directly to the filtered list:

```qml
import QtQuick
import Quickshell

import qs.services

Column {
    spacing: 8

    Repeater {
        model:
            Bluetooth.connectedDeviceList

        delegate: Row {
            required property var modelData

            spacing: 8

            Text {
                text:
                    Bluetooth.deviceIcon(
                        modelData
                    )
            }

            Text {
                text:
                    Bluetooth.displayName(
                        modelData
                    )
            }

            Text {
                visible:
                    modelData.batteryAvailable

                text:
                    Bluetooth.batteryPercent(
                        modelData
                    ).toFixed(0) + "%"
            }
        }
    }
}
```

For a paired-device settings page, use:

```qml
model:
    Bluetooth.pairedDeviceList
```

For a battery-only view, use:

```qml
model:
    Bluetooth.connectedBatteryDeviceList
```

***

## 5.3 Showing the active device and battery

The headline device needs no list scan:

```qml
Text {
    visible:
        Bluetooth.isDeviceConnected

    text:
        Bluetooth.activeDeviceName
}
```

```qml
Text {
    visible:
        Bluetooth.hasDeviceBattery

    text:
        Bluetooth.activeDeviceBatteryText
}
```

The rounded value is useful for progress display:

```qml
ProgressBar {
    visible:
        Bluetooth.hasDeviceBattery

    from: 0
    to: 100

    value:
        Bluetooth.activeDeviceBatteryRounded
}
```

When no device is connected:

```text
activeDevice = null
activeDeviceName = ""
isDeviceConnected = false
hasDeviceBattery = false
activeDeviceBatteryText = ""
```

so gate battery UI on `hasDeviceBattery`.

***

## 5.4 Connecting and disconnecting one device

Connect by address:

```qml
Bluetooth.connectDevice(
    "AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF"
)
```

Disconnect:

```qml
Bluetooth.disconnectDevice(
    "AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF"
)
```

A row button might look like:

```qml
MouseArea {
    anchors.fill:
        parent

    onClicked: {
        if (modelData.connected) {
            Bluetooth.disconnectDevice(
                modelData.address
            )
        } else {
            Bluetooth.connectDevice(
                modelData.address
            )
        }
    }
}
```

Blocked devices refuse to connect. Unblock first:

```qml
Bluetooth.setDeviceBlocked(
    "AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF",
    false
)
```

***

## 5.5 Pairing workflow

Pair a discovered device:

```qml
Bluetooth.pairDevice(
    "AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF"
)
```

Cancel an in-progress pairing:

```qml
Bluetooth.cancelPairDevice(
    "AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF"
)
```

Forget it entirely:

```qml
Bluetooth.forgetDevice(
    "AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF"
)
```

Pairing state can be shown with:

```qml
readonly property string state:
    Bluetooth.deviceStateName(
        device
    )

readonly property bool busy:
    Bluetooth.isDeviceConnecting(
        device
    ) || Bluetooth.isDeviceDisconnecting(
        device
    ) || (device
        ? device.pairing
        : false)
```

***

## 5.6 Device policy controls

Trust a device for easier reconnection:

```qml
Bluetooth.setDeviceTrusted(
    "AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF",
    true
)
```

Block or unblock:

```qml
Bluetooth.setDeviceBlocked(
    "AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF",
    false
)
```

Allow wake from the device:

```qml
Bluetooth.setDeviceWakeAllowed(
    "AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF",
    true
)
```

Rename its alias:

```qml
Bluetooth.setDeviceName(
    "AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF",
    "Headphones"
)
```

Lookup is case-insensitive, so lower-case addresses work.

***

## 5.7 Reacting to adapter and device changes

Log hotplug and discovery results:

```qml
Connections {
    target: Bluetooth

    function onAdapterAdded(adapter) {
        console.log(
            "adapter added:",
            Bluetooth.adapterInfo(adapter).adapterId
        )
    }

    function onAdapterRemoved(adapter) {
        console.log("adapter removed")
    }

    function onDeviceAdded(device) {
        console.log(
            "device found:",
            Bluetooth.displayName(device),
            Bluetooth.deviceStateName(device)
        )
    }

    function onDeviceRemoved(device) {
        console.log("device removed")
    }

    function onDeviceListUpdated() {
        console.log(
            "devices:",
            Bluetooth.deviceCount,
            "connected:",
            Bluetooth.connectedDeviceCount
        )
    }
}
```

Use `adapterListUpdated` for adapter-count UI and `deviceListUpdated` for list refresh side effects.

***

## 5.8 Inspecting serialized state

A developer can inspect one device:

```qml
Text {
    text:
        JSON.stringify(
            Bluetooth.deviceInfo(
                Bluetooth.activeDevice
            ),
            null,
            2
        )
}
```

or the whole service:

```qml
Text {
    text:
        JSON.stringify(
            Bluetooth.statusInfo(),
            null,
            2
        )
}
```

For example:

```json
{
    "isAvailable": true,
    "isEnabled": true,
    "state": "Enabled",
    "adapter": "MyMachine",
    "deviceCount": 3,
    "connectedDeviceCount": 1,
    "activeDevice": "WH-1000XM5",
    "iconKey": "bluetooth-connected"
}
```

This is useful when debugging IPC output or device filtering.

***

## 5.9 Terminal workflow

Inspect the complete service:

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-bluetooth getStatus | jq .
```

Check power and identity:

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-bluetooth getEnabled
```

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-bluetooth getAdapter
```

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-bluetooth getAdapterId
```

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-bluetooth getState
```

Toggle power:

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-bluetooth toggle
```

Scan for devices:

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-bluetooth startDiscovery
```

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-bluetooth getDevices | jq .
```

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-bluetooth stopDiscovery
```

Connect and manage one device:

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-bluetooth connect AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF
```

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-bluetooth getConnectedDevices | jq .
```

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-bluetooth disconnect AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF
```

Pair and trust:

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-bluetooth pair AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF
```

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-bluetooth setTrusted AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF true
```

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-bluetooth forget AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF
```

***

# 6. Detailed architecture

This section is for developers working on `Bluetooth.qml` and the services/components that consume it.

***

## 6.1 Overall architecture

The service is a hardware-state layer over Quickshell Bluetooth.

```text
BlueZ (adapters + Device1 objects)
             │
             ▼
Quickshell.Bluetooth
   ├── Bluetooth.adapters
   ├── Bluetooth.defaultAdapter
   └── Bluetooth.devices
             │
             ▼
N0ctOS Bluetooth.qml
   ├── adapter properties
   ├── ScriptModel filters
   ├── active device
   ├── control functions
   ├── helpers / icons
   └── serialization + IPC
             │
             ▼
N0ctOS Component / terminal
```

There are effectively two responsibilities:

```text
Quickshell.Bluetooth
    BlueZ access and object models

N0ctOS Bluetooth.qml
    shell-friendly properties and actions
```

The N0ctOS service should not reimplement BlueZ discovery, pairing, or D-Bus handling.

***

## 6.2 Backend layer

The backend section exposes Quickshell objects directly:

```text
adapters
adapterList
adapterCount
defaultAdapter
devices
deviceList
deviceCount
```

Derived state is computed from the default adapter:

```text
isAvailable
isEnabled / isPowered
isBlocked
isEnabling
isDisabling
stateName
```

For example:

```text
isAvailable
    =
adapterCount > 0
    AND
defaultAdapter exists
```

and:

```text
stateName
    =
defaultAdapter
    ? BluetoothAdapterState.toString(state)
    : "Disabled"
```

This gives components safe values even on machines without Bluetooth.

***

## 6.3 Default-adapter properties

Adapter identity and mode come from the default adapter:

```text
adapterName
adapterId
adapterDbusPath
isDiscoverable
isDiscovering
isPairable
discoverableTimeout
pairableTimeout
```

Missing hardware returns:

```text
"" for strings
0 for timeouts
false for bools
```

Timeouts are numeric:

```text
Number(adapter.discoverableTimeout)
```

so QML bindings always see an `int`.

***

## 6.4 Filtered device models

Five `ScriptModel` objects filter the global device list:

```text
connectedDeviceModel
    device.connected

pairedDeviceModel
    device.paired

bondedDeviceModel
    device.bonded

batteryDeviceModel
    device.batteryAvailable

connectedBatteryDeviceModel
    device.connected
        AND
    device.batteryAvailable
```

Each filter exposes:

```text
<name>
<name>List
<name>Count
```

For example:

```text
connectedDevices
connectedDeviceList
connectedDeviceCount
```

The filters are reactive: when `deviceList` changes, each model reevaluates.

***

## 6.5 Active device

The active device is derived:

```text
deviceList
    │
    ▼
findFirstConnectedDevice()
    │
    ▼
activeDevice
```

Derived properties follow:

```text
activeDevice
    ├── activeDeviceName = displayName(activeDevice)
    ├── activeDeviceAddress = address
    ├── isDeviceConnected = !!activeDevice
    ├── hasDeviceBattery = batteryAvailable
    ├── activeDeviceBattery = batteryPercent(activeDevice)
    ├── activeDeviceBatteryRounded = round(battery)
    └── activeDeviceBatteryText = rounded + "%"
```

When no device is connected:

```text
activeDevice = null
activeDeviceName = ""
activeDeviceAddress = ""
isDeviceConnected = false
```

***

## 6.6 Signal tracking

Two `Connections` blocks watch adapters:

```text
Bluetooth.onDefaultAdapterChanged
    ↓
stateChangedExternally()
adapterListUpdated()

Bluetooth.adapters.onObjectInsertedPost
    ↓
adapterAdded(adapter)
adapterListUpdated()
stateChangedExternally()

Bluetooth.adapters.onObjectRemovedPost
    ↓
adapterRemoved(adapter)
adapterListUpdated()
stateChangedExternally()
```

One block watches devices:

```text
Bluetooth.devices.onObjectInsertedPost
    ↓
deviceAdded(device)
deviceListUpdated()
stateChangedExternally()

Bluetooth.devices.onObjectRemovedPost
    ↓
deviceRemoved(device)
deviceListUpdated()
stateChangedExternally()
```

Per-device property changes (such as `connected` flipping) flow through Quickshell model reactivity rather than explicit N0ctOS signals.

***

## 6.7 Adapter control semantics

`setEnabled()` is a guarded write:

```text
setEnabled(enabled)
    │
    ▼
defaultAdapter exists?
    │
┌───┴───┐
no     yes
│        │
▼        ▼
return  adapter.enabled = Boolean(enabled)
```

`setDiscoverable()` and `setPairable()` follow the same pattern.

Timeouts clamp negatives:

```text
Math.max(0, Number(seconds))
```

Discovery iterates rather than targeting one adapter:

```text
startDiscovery
    │
    ▼
for each adapter
    │
    ▼
enabled?
    │
┌───┴───┐
no     yes
│        │
▼        ▼
skip   discovering = true
```

```text
stopDiscovery
    │
    ▼
for each adapter
    discovering = false
```

***

## 6.8 Device lookup semantics

`findDevice()` normalizes both sides:

```text
String(address || "")
    ↓
lowercase compare
    ↓
device.address
```

Empty input returns:

```text
null
```

`findDeviceByName()` compares resolved display names:

```text
displayName(device).toLowerCase()
    ===
wanted.toLowerCase()
```

This means a search for:

```text
wh-1000xm5
```

finds:

```text
WH-1000XM5
```

***

## 6.9 Connection and pairing guards

Connection refuses blocked hardware:

```text
connectDevice(address)
    │
    ▼
findDevice()
    │
┌───┴───┐
null   found
│        │
▼        ▼
return  blocked?
            │
        ┌───┴───┐
       yes      no
        │        │
        ▼        ▼
      return  device.connect()
```

Pairing has three guards:

```text
pairDevice(address)
    │
    ▼
unknown -> return
paired -> return
pairing -> return
    │
    ▼
device.pair()
```

Cancellation is the inverse:

```text
cancelPairDevice(address)
    │
    ▼
not pairing -> return
    │
    ▼
device.cancelPair()
```

`disconnectDevice()` and `forgetDevice()` only guard unknown addresses.

***

## 6.10 Policy control

Policy writes are thin wrappers:

```text
setDeviceTrusted(address, trusted)
    → device.trusted = Boolean(trusted)

setDeviceBlocked(address, blocked)
    → device.blocked = Boolean(blocked)

setDeviceWakeAllowed(address, allowed)
    → device.wakeAllowed = Boolean(allowed)

setDeviceName(address, name)
    → device.name = String(name || "")
```

Each one returns silently when the address is unknown.

***

## 6.11 Display and battery helpers

`displayName()` implements:

```text
device = null -> ""
name.trim() !== "" -> name
otherwise -> deviceName
otherwise -> ""
```

`batteryPercent()` implements:

```text
null -> 0
!batteryAvailable -> 0
non-finite -> 0
otherwise -> clamp(value * 100, 0, 100)
```

The multiplication exists because Quickshell uses:

```text
0.0 -> 1.0
```

while the shell uses:

```text
0 -> 100
```

***

## 6.12 Device state helpers

`deviceStateName()` wraps:

```qml
BluetoothDeviceState.toString(
    device.state
)
```

and returns `"Unknown"` for null.

Connection transitions expose:

```text
isDeviceConnecting
    state === Connecting

isDeviceDisconnecting
    state === Disconnecting
```

These are useful for spinners and disabled buttons during BlueZ transitions.

***

## 6.13 Icon mapping

Device icon keys match substrings in:

```text
(device.icon + " " + displayName).toLowerCase()
```

The match order is:

```text
headset / headphone / earbud -> headphones
speaker -> speaker
keyboard -> keyboard
mouse -> mouse
gamepad / joystick -> gamepad
phone / smartphone -> phone
tablet -> tablet
computer / laptop -> laptop
printer -> printer
camera -> camera
tv / display -> television
otherwise -> bluetooth
```

`deviceIcon()` maps each key to one glyph.

Adapter icons use priority order:

```text
!isAvailable -> off
isBlocked -> off
isDisabling -> off
isEnabling -> on
isDiscovering -> on
connectedDeviceCount > 0 -> connected
isEnabled -> on
otherwise -> off
```

Icon keys use stable names for theming:

```text
bluetooth-off
bluetooth-blocked
bluetooth-discovering
bluetooth-connected
bluetooth
```

***

## 6.14 Serialization architecture

Serializers convert live Quickshell objects into plain data:

```text
live device object
    │
    ▼
deviceInfo()
    │
    ▼
plain object
    │
    ▼
JSON.stringify for IPC
```

`deviceInfo()` includes:

```text
name
deviceName
address
dbusPath
adapter
adapterName
state
isConnected
isConnecting
isDisconnecting
isPaired
isBonded
isPairing
isTrusted
isBlocked
isWakeAllowed
isBatteryAvailable
battery
batteryRounded
batteryText
icon
iconKey
```

`adapterInfo()` includes its own connected-device snapshots:

```text
adapter.devices.values
    ↓
filter connected
    ↓
deviceInfo(each)
    ↓
connectedDevices[]
```

`statusInfo()` aggregates headline state plus counts:

```text
adapter state
discovery state
adapterCount
deviceCount
connectedDeviceCount
pairedDeviceCount
bondedDeviceCount
batteryDeviceCount
activeDevice
icon
iconKey
```

***

## 6.15 Discovery lifecycle

A full scan follows:

```text
startDiscovery()
        │
        ▼
enabled adapters discovering = true
        │
        ▼
BlueZ reports devices
        │
        ▼
Bluetooth.devices inserts objects
        │
        ▼
deviceAdded()
deviceListUpdated()
        │
        ▼
filtered models reevaluate
        │
        ▼
stopDiscovery()
        │
        ▼
adapters discovering = false
```

Components should start discovery when a Bluetooth page opens and stop it when the page closes.

***

## 6.16 Connection lifecycle

A connection follows:

```text
connectDevice(address)
        │
        ▼
device.connect()
        │
        ▼
device.state = Connecting
        │
        ▼
device.connected = true
        │
        ▼
connectedDeviceList changes
        │
        ▼
activeDevice may change
        │
        ▼
icon may change to connected
```

Disconnection follows the reverse path and may clear `activeDevice`.

***

## 6.17 Pairing lifecycle

Pairing follows:

```text
pairDevice(address)
        │
        ▼
device.pair()
        │
        ▼
device.pairing = true
        │
        ▼
BlueZ agent / confirmation
        │
        ▼
device.paired = true
device.pairing = false
```

Cancellation interrupts it:

```text
cancelPairDevice(address)
        │
        ▼
device.cancelPair()
        │
        ▼
device.pairing = false
```

Forgetting removes the object:

```text
forgetDevice(address)
        │
        ▼
device.forget()
        │
        ▼
deviceRemoved()
```

***

## 6.18 IPC architecture

IPC is a thin external interface over the same service API.

Conceptually:

```text
terminal
   │
   ▼
n0ctos-bluetooth
   │
   ▼
Bluetooth.qml
   │
   ▼
Quickshell.Bluetooth
   │
   ▼
BlueZ
```

For example:

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-bluetooth connect AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF
```

becomes conceptually:

```qml
Bluetooth.connectDevice(
    "AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF"
)
```

The IPC layer serializes bools as `"true"`/`"false"` strings and device lists as JSON strings.

***

## 6.19 Why IPC stays high-level

IPC should expose useful Bluetooth operations, not internal implementation.

External callers do not need to know about:

```text
raw ObjectModel
ScriptModel filters
Connections handlers
battery 0.0 -> 1.0 conversion
icon substring matching
first-connected resolution
```

They only need:

```text
getStatus
getState
getEnabled / setEnabled / toggle
startDiscovery / stopDiscovery
getDevices
connect / disconnect
pair / cancelPair / forget
setTrusted / setBlocked / setWakeAllowed / setName
```

This keeps the IPC interface stable even if the internal filtering changes.

***

## 6.20 Performance model

Bluetooth is intended to be cheap during normal UI operation.

A component read such as:

```qml
Bluetooth.connectedDeviceCount
```

does not perform D-Bus I/O.

D-Bus is handled by Quickshell.

The N0ctOS service operates on already-loaded reactive models.

Normal runtime work is therefore:

```text
QML binding
    ↓
Bluetooth
    ↓
in-memory model lookup
```

rather than:

```text
QML binding
    ↓
D-Bus
    ↓
BlueZ scan
    ↓
lookup
```

***

## 6.21 No polling

Bluetooth does not use a polling timer to detect devices.

There is no:

```qml
Timer {
    interval: 1000
    repeat: true

    onTriggered:
        reloadBluetooth()
}
```

Changes propagate through Quickshell's reactive Bluetooth models.

This avoids unnecessary CPU and radio activity.

***

## 6.22 Service boundaries

The responsibilities are intentionally divided:

```text
N0ctOS Bluetooth.qml
    adapter properties
    filtered collections
    active device
    control actions
    display and icon helpers
    serialization
    IPC

Quickshell.Bluetooth
    adapter objects
    device objects
    D-Bus communication
    discovery implementation
    connection implementation

BlueZ
    hardware control
    pairing state
    audio and HID handling
```

N0ctOS code should not duplicate BlueZ protocol handling.

***

## 6.23 No Config ownership

Unlike configuration services, Bluetooth owns no config section.

There is no:

```text
bluetooth.profile
bluetooth.settings
homeConfig section
```

Device trust, pairing, and adapter power live in BlueZ.

The service is therefore stateless across restarts except for what BlueZ itself remembers.

***

## 6.24 What UI / service code should not do

Components should not:

```text
import Quickshell.Bluetooth directly for common tasks

scan Bluetooth.devices.values manually when a filter exists

reimplement battery 0.0 -> 100 conversion

reimplement display-name fallback

reimplement device icon matching

mutate deviceInfo() output and expect hardware changes

assume activeDevice is non-null

assume an adapter always exists

poll BlueZ on a timer
```

Instead:

```qml
Bluetooth.isEnabled
Bluetooth.connectedDeviceList
Bluetooth.activeDeviceName
Bluetooth.batteryPercent(device)
Bluetooth.displayName(device)
Bluetooth.deviceIcon(device)
Bluetooth.connectDevice(address)
Bluetooth.deviceInfo(device)
```

should be the normal interface.

***

## 6.25 Final architecture summary

The entire system can be viewed as:

```text
                         Component
                            │
                            │ properties / actions
                            ▼
                    ┌─────────────────┐
                    │    Bluetooth    │
                    │                 │
                    │ adapter state   │
                    │ device filters  │
                    │ active device   │
                    │ control         │
                    │ helpers / icons │
                    │ serialization   │
                    │ IPC             │
                    └────────┬────────┘
                             │
                             │ Quickshell API
                             ▼
                    ┌─────────────────┐
                    │ Quickshell      │
                    │ Bluetooth       │
                    │                 │
                    │ adapters        │
                    │ devices         │
                    │ D-Bus / BlueZ   │
                    └────────┬────────┘
                             │
                             ▼
                            BlueZ
```

The core rule is:

> **Components describe what Bluetooth state or action they need; `Bluetooth.qml` resolves it from Quickshell models and BlueZ; Quickshell handles how hardware communication actually happens.**


# Brightness Service



`Brightness.qml` is N0ctOS's centralized backlight and LED brightness service.

It gives every shell component one consistent place to read and control display and keyboard brightness without touching `brightnessctl` or `sysfs` directly.

The service supports automatic device discovery, per-device `sysfs` tracking, active-device selection, percent normalization, clamped absolute sets, stepwise increase/decrease, per-device convenience controls, and a read/write IPC interface.

The normal usage pattern is:

```text
Component
    │
    ▼
Brightness
    │
    ├── active device
    ├── device list
    └── resolved percent + text
    │
    ▼
brightnessctl / sysfs
    │
    ▼
backlight + LED hardware
```

***

# 1. What does it do?

`Brightness.qml` exposes the current brightness for the shell.

A component can read a simple value:

```qml
Brightness.percentText
```

or a simple state flag:

```qml
Brightness.hasDevice
```

or drive the active display:

```qml
Brightness.increase(
    Brightness.device,
    5
)
```

More detailed state is also available:

```json
{
    "key": "backlight:intel_backlight",
    "name": "intel_backlight",
    "type": "backlight",
    "value": 1200,
    "max": 4800,
    "percent": 25,
    "percentText": "25%",
    "sysfsPath": "/sys/class/backlight/intel_backlight",
    "selected": true
}
```

The effective percent is resolved in this order:

```text
sysfs brightness / sysfs max_brightness
    ↓
clamp 0 -> 100
    ↓
device.percent / percentRounded / percentText
    ↓
Brightness.percent / percentRounded / percentText (active device)
```

So a component can simply do:

```qml
Text {
    text:
        Brightness.percentText
}
```

and not care which backlight or LED the value came from.

If no brightness hardware exists, the service returns safe fallbacks (`0`, `""`, `false`, `null`) instead of failing.

***

# 2. UI API

Import normally:

```qml
import QtQuick
import Quickshell

import qs.services
```

## Core API

| How to read                 | What does it do                                                                                        |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `Brightness.isAvailable`    | `true` once `brightnessctl` discovery has succeeded. `false` before discovery or when discovery fails. |
| `Brightness.isDiscovering`  | `true` while the discovery `Process` is running.                                                       |
| `Brightness.devices`        | Copy of all discovered devices (`_devices.slice()`).                                                   |
| `Brightness.backlights`     | Devices whose class is `backlight`.                                                                    |
| `Brightness.leds`           | Devices whose class is `leds`.                                                                         |
| `Brightness.count`          | Number of discovered devices.                                                                          |
| `Brightness.backlightCount` | Number of backlight devices.                                                                           |
| `Brightness.ledCount`       | Number of LED devices.                                                                                 |
| `Brightness.defaultDevice`  | First backlight, otherwise first device, otherwise `null`.                                             |
| `Brightness.device`         | Active device: selected device when it still exists, otherwise `defaultDevice`.                        |
| `Brightness.hasDevice`      | `true` when an active device exists.                                                                   |
| `Brightness.value`          | Raw `brightness` integer of the active device, `0` when none.                                          |
| `Brightness.max`            | Raw `max_brightness` integer of the active device, `0` when none.                                      |
| `Brightness.percent`        | Active-device percent `0 -> 100`, clamped, `0` when none or `max <= 0`.                                |
| `Brightness.percentRounded` | `Math.round(percent)`.                                                                                 |
| `Brightness.percentText`    | `"25%"` style text.                                                                                    |
| `Brightness.deviceName`     | Active-device `name` (`deviceId`), `""` when none.                                                     |
| `Brightness.deviceKey`      | Active-device `key` (`"class:id"`), `""` when none.                                                    |

Each entry in `devices`, `backlights`, `leds`, `device`, and `defaultDevice` is a device object with:

| How to read             | What does it do                                               |
| ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `device.key`            | `"class:id"`, for example `"backlight:intel_backlight"`.      |
| `device.deviceId`       | Kernel device id, for example `"intel_backlight"`.            |
| `device.deviceClass`    | Kernel class, `"backlight"` or `"leds"`.                      |
| `device.sysfsPath`      | `"/sys/class/<class>/<id>"`.                                  |
| `device.name`           | Same as `deviceId`.                                           |
| `device.className`      | Same as `deviceClass`.                                        |
| `device.displayName`    | Same as `deviceId`.                                           |
| `device.type`           | `"backlight"` or `"led"`.                                     |
| `device.isBacklight`    | `true` when `deviceClass === "backlight"`.                    |
| `device.isLed`          | `true` when `deviceClass === "leds"`.                         |
| `device.value`          | Raw `brightness` integer, `0` initially.                      |
| `device.max`            | Raw `max_brightness` integer, `0` initially.                  |
| `device.isPresent`      | `true` when the `brightness` `FileView` exists and is loaded. |
| `device.percent`        | `value * 100 / max`, clamped `0 -> 100`, `0` when `max <= 0`. |
| `device.percentRounded` | `Math.round(device.percent)`.                                 |
| `device.percentText`    | `"25%"` style text for that device.                           |

## Helpers

| How to call                                 | What does it do                                                                                                                                                           |
| ------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Brightness.refresh()`                      | Re-runs `brightnessctl --list --machine-readable` unless discovery is already running.                                                                                    |
| `Brightness.deviceForKey(key)`              | Returns the device with `"class:id"` key, or `null` when missing, empty, or null.                                                                                         |
| `Brightness.deviceFor(className, deviceId)` | Convenience for `deviceForKey(className + ":" + deviceId)`.                                                                                                               |
| `Brightness.findDefaultDevice()`            | First backlight, otherwise first device, otherwise `null`.                                                                                                                |
| `Brightness.resolveDevice(value)`           | Accepts a service device object or a `"class:id"` string and returns the live service device, or `null`. Rejects foreign objects.                                         |
| `Brightness.set(device, value)`             | Clamps `value` to `0 -> 100` and runs `brightnessctl set <percent>%`. Returns `true` when the operation starts, `false` when there is no target or `value` is non-finite. |
| `Brightness.increase(device, amount)`       | Runs `brightnessctl set +<step>%`. `step` defaults to `5` when `amount` is missing, non-finite, or `<= 0`. Returns `true`/`false` like `set()`.                           |
| `Brightness.decrease(device, amount)`       | Runs `brightnessctl set -<step>%`. Same defaulting and return rules as `increase()`.                                                                                      |
| `Brightness.setDevice(key)`                 | Selects the active device by key. Returns `true` and stores `_selectedKey`, `false` when the key is unknown.                                                              |
| `Brightness.resetDevice()`                  | Clears the selection so the active device falls back to `defaultDevice`. Always returns `true`.                                                                           |
| `Brightness.deviceInfo(device)`             | Returns a plain JSON-safe info object for one device, `{}` when null. `percent` is the rounded integer.                                                                   |
| `Brightness.readInteger(value)`             | Parses a `sysfs` string with `parseInt`, `0` when non-finite, clamped to `>= 0`.                                                                                          |
| `Brightness.clearDevices()`                 | Destroys all device objects, empties the list, and clears the selection.                                                                                                  |
| `Brightness.applyDiscovery(lines)`          | Parses discovery lines and creates, retains, or destroys device objects.                                                                                                  |
| `Brightness.runOperation(device, value)`    | Spawns one short-lived `brightnessctl set` process for `device`. Returns `true` when started, `false` when there is no device or the process cannot be created.           |

Per-device convenience wrappers call back into the service with that device:

| How to call               | What does it do                                                                         |
| ------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `device.set(value)`       | Same as `Brightness.set(device, value)`.                                                |
| `device.increase(amount)` | Same as `Brightness.increase(device, amount)`.                                          |
| `device.decrease(amount)` | Same as `Brightness.decrease(device, amount)`.                                          |
| `device.refresh()`        | Reloads that device's `brightness` and `max_brightness` `FileView` objects when loaded. |

| Example                                                | Result                                                                   |
| ------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `Brightness.set(Brightness.device, 70)`                | `true`, starts `brightnessctl set 70%` on the active device              |
| `Brightness.set("backlight:intel_backlight", 70)`      | `true` when that device exists, `false` when it does not                 |
| `Brightness.set(Brightness.device, 150)`               | `true`, clamped to `100%`, starts `brightnessctl set 100%`               |
| `Brightness.increase(Brightness.device, 5)`            | `true`, starts `brightnessctl set +5%`                                   |
| `Brightness.decrease(Brightness.device, 5)`            | `true`, starts `brightnessctl set -5%`                                   |
| `Brightness.increase(Brightness.device, 0)`            | `true`, invalid step falls back to `5`, starts `brightnessctl set +5%`   |
| `Brightness.deviceForKey("backlight:intel_backlight")` | Live device object, or `null` when missing or empty                      |
| `Brightness.deviceFor("backlight", "intel_backlight")` | Live device object, or `null` when missing                               |
| `Brightness.resolveDevice(Brightness.device)`          | The same live service device, or `null` when it no longer exists         |
| `Brightness.setDevice("backlight:intel_backlight")`    | `true` and the active device changes, or `false` when the key is unknown |
| `Brightness.deviceInfo(Brightness.device)`             | `{key, value, max, percent, ...}` info object, `{}` when null            |

### Typical component usage

```qml
Text {
    text:
        Brightness.percentText
}

Text {
    visible:
        Brightness.hasDevice

    text:
        Brightness.deviceName +
        ": " +
        Brightness.percentText
}

MouseArea {
    onWheel: (wheel) => {
        if (wheel.angleDelta.y > 0)
            Brightness.increase(
                Brightness.device,
                5
            )
        else
            Brightness.decrease(
                Brightness.device,
                5
            )
    }
}
```

That is the intended everyday usage.

Components normally should not need to know how `brightnessctl` discovery, `sysfs` watchers, keys, or default-device selection work.

***

# 3. IPC API

IPC target:

```text
n0ctos-brightness
```

## State reads

| How to call     | What does it do                                                   |
| --------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `isAvailable`   | Returns `isAvailable`.                                            |
| `isDiscovering` | Returns `isDiscovering`.                                          |
| `hasDevice`     | Returns `hasDevice`.                                              |
| `count`         | Returns `count`.                                                  |
| `get`           | Returns `percentText`, e.g. `"25%"`.                              |
| `getValue`      | Returns raw `value` of the active device.                         |
| `getMax`        | Returns raw `max` of the active device.                           |
| `getDeviceName` | Returns `deviceName`, e.g. `"intel_backlight"`, or `""`.          |
| `getDeviceKey`  | Returns `deviceKey`, e.g. `"backlight:intel_backlight"`, or `""`. |
| `getDefault`    | Returns the default-device key, or `""` when none.                |
| `getDevice`     | Returns the active device as a JSON string, or `""` when none.    |

| Example                                       | Result                                                    |
| --------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| `qs ipc call n0ctos-brightness isAvailable`   | `true` when discovery has succeeded, `false` otherwise    |
| `qs ipc call n0ctos-brightness hasDevice`     | `true` when an active device exists                       |
| `qs ipc call n0ctos-brightness count`         | `2`, the number of discovered devices                     |
| `qs ipc call n0ctos-brightness get`           | `"25%"`, the active-device text                           |
| `qs ipc call n0ctos-brightness getValue`      | `1200`, the raw `brightness` integer                      |
| `qs ipc call n0ctos-brightness getMax`        | `4800`, the raw `max_brightness` integer                  |
| `qs ipc call n0ctos-brightness getDeviceName` | `"intel_backlight"`, or `""` when none                    |
| `qs ipc call n0ctos-brightness getDeviceKey`  | `"backlight:intel_backlight"`, or `""` when none          |
| `qs ipc call n0ctos-brightness getDefault`    | `"backlight:intel_backlight"`, or `""` when none          |
| `qs ipc call n0ctos-brightness getDevice`     | JSON info object for the active device, or `""` when none |

For example:

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-brightness get
```

returns:

```text
25%
```

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-brightness getDeviceKey
```

returns:

```text
backlight:intel_backlight
```

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-brightness getValue
```

returns:

```text
1200
```

## Device lists

| How to call  | What does it do                                                 |
| ------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `list`       | Returns one info object per discovered device as a JSON string. |
| `backlights` | Returns only backlight devices as a JSON string.                |
| `leds`       | Returns only LED devices as a JSON string.                      |

| Example                                    | Result                                     |
| ------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------ |
| `qs ipc call n0ctos-brightness list`       | JSON array with one info object per device |
| `qs ipc call n0ctos-brightness backlights` | JSON array with only backlight devices     |
| `qs ipc call n0ctos-brightness leds`       | JSON array with only LED devices           |

`list` returns:

```json
[
    {
        "key": "backlight:intel_backlight",
        "id": "intel_backlight",
        "class": "backlight",
        "name": "intel_backlight",
        "displayName": "intel_backlight",
        "type": "backlight",
        "isBacklight": true,
        "isLed": false,
        "isPresent": true,
        "value": 1200,
        "max": 4800,
        "percent": 25,
        "percentText": "25%",
        "sysfsPath": "/sys/class/backlight/intel_backlight",
        "selected": true
    }
]
```

With no devices, `list` returns:

```json
[]
```

## Current-device writes

These act on the active device:

| How to call          | What does it do                                                                    |
| -------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `set <percent>`      | Sets the active device to `<percent>`, clamped `0 -> 100`. Returns `true`/`false`. |
| `increase <percent>` | Increases the active device by `<percent>`, default `5`. Returns `true`/`false`.   |
| `decrease <percent>` | Decreases the active device by `<percent>`, default `5`. Returns `true`/`false`.   |

| Example                                    | Result                                                      |
| ------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `qs ipc call n0ctos-brightness set 70`     | `true`, starts `brightnessctl set 70%` on the active device |
| `qs ipc call n0ctos-brightness increase 5` | `true`, starts `brightnessctl set +5%`                      |
| `qs ipc call n0ctos-brightness decrease 5` | `true`, starts `brightnessctl set -5%`                      |

For example:

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-brightness set 70
```

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-brightness increase 5
```

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-brightness decrease 5
```

A missing or invalid step falls back to `5`:

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-brightness increase 0
```

still steps by `5%` and returns `true` when a device exists.

## Specific-device writes and selection

| How to call                      | What does it do                                                                                 |
| -------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `setDevice <key>`                | Selects the active device by `"class:id"` key. Returns `true` on success, `false` when unknown. |
| `resetDevice`                    | Clears the selection so the active device falls back to the default. Always returns `true`.     |
| `setDeviceValue <key> <percent>` | Sets one device by key, clamped `0 -> 100`. Returns `true`/`false`.                             |
| `increaseDevice <key> <percent>` | Increases one device by key, default `5`. Returns `true`/`false`.                               |
| `decreaseDevice <key> <percent>` | Decreases one device by key, default `5`. Returns `true`/`false`.                               |

| Example                                                                     | Result                                                                |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `qs ipc call n0ctos-brightness setDevice backlight:intel_backlight`         | `true` and the active device changes, `false` when the key is unknown |
| `qs ipc call n0ctos-brightness resetDevice`                                 | `true`, selection cleared, active device falls back to default        |
| `qs ipc call n0ctos-brightness setDeviceValue backlight:intel_backlight 70` | `true` when that device exists, `false` otherwise                     |
| `qs ipc call n0ctos-brightness increaseDevice backlight:intel_backlight 5`  | `true` when that device exists, `false` otherwise                     |
| `qs ipc call n0ctos-brightness decreaseDevice backlight:intel_backlight 5`  | `true` when that device exists, `false` otherwise                     |

For example:

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-brightness setDevice backlight:intel_backlight
```

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-brightness setDeviceValue backlight:intel_backlight 70
```

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-brightness resetDevice
```

## Discovery

| How to call | What does it do                                                  |
| ----------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `refresh`   | Re-runs discovery unless it is already running. Returns nothing. |

| Example                                 | Result                                        |
| --------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| `qs ipc call n0ctos-brightness refresh` | No return value, discovery restarts when idle |

For example:

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-brightness refresh
```

***

# 4. Features / limitations

## Features

### Automatic discovery through `brightnessctl`

Discovery runs:

```text
brightnessctl --list --machine-readable
```

Each output line has the form:

```text
DEVICE,CLASS,CURRENT,PERCENT,MAX
```

For example:

```text
intel_backlight,backlight,1200,25%,4800
```

`applyDiscovery()` splits each line on commas, requires at least 5 parts with a non-empty device id and class, deduplicates by `"class:id"`, and then creates, retains, or destroys device objects.

Malformed and blank lines are skipped.

### Backlight and LED separation

The full list is split by class:

```text
_devices
    ↓
isBacklight -> backlights
isLed       -> leds
```

A panel can therefore bind to only real displays:

```qml
Brightness.backlights
```

or only keyboard/status LEDs:

```qml
Brightness.leds
```

### Active and default device

The default prefers a real display:

```text
first backlight
    ↓
otherwise first brightness device
    ↓
otherwise null
```

The active device prefers an explicit selection:

```text
selected key still exists -> selected device
otherwise                 -> default device
```

This gives sliders and keys stable bindings without tracking hotplug manually.

### `sysfs` tracking without polling

Each device owns two `FileView` objects:

```text
/sys/class/<class>/<id>/brightness (watched)
/sys/class/<class>/<id>/max_brightness (unwatched)
```

The current-brightness file uses:

```qml
watchChanges: true
```

and reloads on `fileChanged()`, because `FileView` does not reload automatically.

The max-brightness file uses:

```qml
watchChanges: false
```

because the maximum rarely changes.

External changes through keys, `brightnessctl`, or desktop controls therefore appear through file notifications, not a timer.

### Percent normalization

Raw `sysfs` integers become UI-ready percent:

```text
max > 0 ? clamp(value * 100 / max, 0, 100) : 0
    ↓
percent
    ↓
round -> percentRounded
    ↓
String + "%" -> percentText
```

`deviceInfo().percent` is the rounded integer, matching `percentRounded`.

### Clamped absolute sets

`set()` converts its argument with `Number()`, rejects non-finite input with `false`, and clamps:

```text
clamp(value, 0, 100)
    ↓
brightnessctl set <percent>%
```

So:

```qml
Brightness.set(
    Brightness.device,
    150
)
```

targets `100%`, and a negative value targets `0%`.

### Stepwise control with a safe default

`increase()` and `decrease()` convert `amount` with `Number()` and fall back:

```text
missing / non-finite / <= 0
    ↓
step = 5
```

They then run:

```text
brightnessctl set +<step>%
brightnessctl set -<step>%
```

Key bindings can therefore omit the step or pass `0` safely.

### Per-device convenience

A device object forwards to the service:

```qml
device.set(70)
device.increase(5)
device.decrease(5)
```

These are the same operations as:

```qml
Brightness.set(device, 70)
Brightness.increase(device, 5)
Brightness.decrease(device, 5)
```

but read naturally inside delegates and loops.

### Immediate refresh after control

Each `set`, `increase`, and `decrease` spawns its own short-lived `Process`:

```text
brightnessctl --quiet --class <class> --device <id> set <value>
```

On exit the target device calls:

```qml
device.refresh()
```

so the `sysfs` value is reloaded immediately without waiting for the next file notification.

### Safe empty-hardware fallbacks

With no devices:

```text
hasDevice = false
device = null
defaultDevice = null
value = 0
max = 0
percent = 0
percentRounded = 0
percentText = "0%"
deviceName = ""
deviceKey = ""
count = 0
devices = []
```

Components can bind directly without null checks on every property.

### JSON-safe device info

`deviceInfo()` converts one live device into plain data with:

```text
key / id / class / name / displayName
type / isBacklight / isLed / isPresent
value / max / percent / percentText
sysfsPath / selected
```

The same function backs IPC `list`, `backlights`, `leds`, and `getDevice()`.

***

## Limitations

### `brightnessctl` is required

If:

```text
brightnessctl --list --machine-readable
```

exits non-zero, the service sets:

```text
_available = false
```

and logs:

```text
[Brightness] brightnessctl discovery failed
```

No devices are committed in that case. The shell must have `brightnessctl` installed and permission to access backlight devices.

### Device selection is runtime-only

`_selectedKey` is intentionally not persisted yet:

```qml
property string _selectedKey: ""
```

Restarting the shell clears the selection. If the selected key disappears during a later discovery, it is cleared automatically and the active device falls back to the default.

### Writes are asynchronous

`set()`, `increase()`, and `decrease()` return:

```text
true  -> process started
false -> no target / bad input / process creation failed
```

`true` does not mean the hardware already changed. The `sysfs` value updates when `brightnessctl` exits and the device refreshes, or when the file watcher fires.

### `resolveDevice()` only accepts service devices

An object is accepted only when it has a usable `key` that matches a live device:

```text
foreign {key: "..."} -> null
removed device       -> null
unknown string       -> null
empty string         -> null
null / undefined     -> null
```

This prevents an arbitrary QML object with a `key` property from being sent to `brightnessctl`.

### `FileView` failures are warnings, not fatal

A missing `sysfs` file logs:

```text
[Brightness] failed to load brightness file
[Brightness] failed to load max-brightness file
```

The device still exists in the list, but:

```text
isPresent = false
value may stay 0
max may stay 0
percent = 0
```

Callers should check `hasDevice` or `isPresent` when accuracy matters.

### `percent` in `deviceInfo()` is rounded

The info object reports:

```qml
percent: device.percentRounded
```

not the raw float. A device at `24.6%` reports:

```json
{
    "percent": 25,
    "percentText": "25%"
}
```

Use `device.percent` directly in QML when the unrounded value is needed.

***

# 5. Example use cases

## 5.1 A panel showing brightness

A panel only needs two bindings:

```qml
import QtQuick
import Quickshell

import qs.services

Row {
    spacing: 6

    Text {
        visible:
            Brightness.hasDevice

        text:
            Brightness.percentText
    }

    Text {
        visible:
            !Brightness.hasDevice

        text:
            "No backlight"
    }
}
```

The component does not need to know whether the value came from:

```text
a laptop display backlight
a fallback first device
an explicitly selected LED
no hardware at all
```

It only receives the effective value.

***

## 5.2 A slider setting absolute brightness

`set()` takes the active device plus a percent:

```qml
import QtQuick

import qs.services

Slider {
    enabled:
        Brightness.hasDevice

    from: 0
    to: 100

    value:
        Brightness.percent

    onMoved: {
        Brightness.set(
            Brightness.device,
            value
        )
    }
}
```

Out-of-range slider values are clamped by the service, so no manual `Math.max`/`Math.min` is needed.

The same works through a key string:

```qml
Brightness.set(
    "backlight:intel_backlight",
    70
)
```

which returns `false` when that device does not exist.

***

## 5.3 Brightness keys stepping up and down

Step functions default to `5` when the amount is missing or invalid:

```qml
import QtQuick

import qs.services

Item {
    focus: true

    Keys.onPressed: (event) => {
        if (event.key === Qt.Key_MonBrightnessUp) {
            Brightness.increase(
                Brightness.device,
                5
            )

            event.accepted = true
        } else if (event.key === Qt.Key_MonBrightnessDown) {
            Brightness.decrease(
                Brightness.device,
                5
            )

            event.accepted = true
        }
    }
}
```

The result is:

```text
increase 5 -> brightnessctl set +5%
decrease 5 -> brightnessctl set -5%
missing / 0 / negative -> +5% / -5%
```

***

## 5.4 Listing devices and selecting one

`devices` is a plain array copy, so it works with `Repeater` and loops:

```qml
import QtQuick

import qs.services

Column {
    spacing: 8

    Repeater {
        model:
            Brightness.devices

        delegate: Text {
            required property var modelData

            text:
                Brightness.deviceInfo(
                    modelData
                ).key +
                ": " +
                Brightness.deviceInfo(
                    modelData
                ).percentText

            color:
                Brightness.deviceInfo(
                    modelData
                ).selected
                    ? "#2acfff"
                    : "#ffffff"

            MouseArea {
                anchors.fill:
                    parent

                onClicked:
                    Brightness.setDevice(
                        parent.modelData.key
                    )
            }
        }
    }
}
```

For imperative code, use the lookup helpers:

```qml
const panel =
    Brightness.deviceFor(
        "backlight",
        "intel_backlight"
    )

if (panel)
    Brightness.setDevice(
        panel.key
    )
else
    Brightness.resetDevice()
```

`setDevice()` returns `false` for an unknown key and leaves the selection unchanged.

***

## 5.5 Terminal workflow

Read the active brightness:

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-brightness get
```

Read the active key:

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-brightness getDeviceKey
```

List every device:

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-brightness list
```

List only backlights:

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-brightness backlights
```

Set the active device:

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-brightness set 70
```

Step the active device:

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-brightness increase 5
qs ipc call n0ctos-brightness decrease 5
```

Target one device:

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-brightness setDeviceValue backlight:intel_backlight 70
```

Select that device for subsequent `set` calls:

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-brightness setDevice backlight:intel_backlight
```

Return to the default device:

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-brightness resetDevice
```

Re-run discovery:

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-brightness refresh
```

Inspect the complete service:

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-brightness getDevice
```

***

# 6. Detailed architecture

This section is for developers working on `Brightness.qml` and the services/components that consume it.

***

## 6.1 Overall architecture

The service is a normalization and control layer built on top of `brightnessctl` and `sysfs` file watching.

```text
N0ctOS Component / Service
            │
            ▼
      Brightness.qml
            │
     ┌──────┼────────┐
     │      │        │
     ▼      ▼        ▼
 discovery sysfs   control
  list    FileView process
     │      │        │
     └──────┴────────┘
            │
            ▼
  brightnessctl / sysfs
            │
            ▼
 backlight + LED hardware
```

There are effectively two responsibilities:

```text
Brightness
    N0ctOS-friendly discovery, normalization, and selection

brightnessctl / sysfs
    hardware enumeration and actual brightness changes
```

Brightness should not duplicate the hardware access already provided by those layers.

***

## 6.2 Configuration structure

The service owns no `Config` section.

There is no:

```json
{
    "brightness": {
        "device": "...",
        "percent": 70
    }
}
```

Device selection lives only in memory:

```qml
property string _selectedKey: ""
```

Device values live in `sysfs`, not in N0ctOS configuration files.

***

## 6.3 Discovery input

Discovery runs:

```text
brightnessctl --list --machine-readable
```

The expected line format is:

```text
DEVICE,CLASS,CURRENT,PERCENT,MAX
```

For example:

```text
intel_backlight,backlight,1200,25%,4800
asus::kbd_backlight,leds,1,33%,3
```

Only `DEVICE` and `CLASS` are used for identity. `CURRENT` and `MAX` are read later through `sysfs`, so discovery stays stable even if the values change between listing and watching.

***

## 6.4 Discovery parsing

`applyDiscovery()` performs:

```text
trim line
    ↓
skip empty
    ↓
split on ","
    ↓
require >= 5 parts
    ↓
require non-empty id + class
    ↓
key = class + ":" + id
    ↓
deduplicate by key
```

Deduplication uses a plain object as a set:

```text
seen[key] = true
```

so a duplicated `brightnessctl` line cannot create two device objects.

***

## 6.5 Create and retain

Existing devices are indexed by key:

```text
existing[device.key] = device
```

Each discovered entry then either:

```text
exists -> retain object
missing -> createObject + two FileViews
```

Retained objects keep their:

```text
FileView instances
value / max
bindings
```

so a periodic `refresh()` does not destroy and recreate stable devices.

***

## 6.6 Removal

Devices absent from the new discovery are destroyed:

```text
old device not in nextDevices
    ↓
oldDevice.destroy()
    ↓
FileView children destroyed too
```

because the `FileView` objects are QObject children of the device.

The service logs:

```text
[Brightness] removed: <key>
```

If the removed device was selected, `_selectedKey` is cleared so the active device falls back to the default.

***

## 6.7 `sysfs` file layer

Each new device gets:

```text
<sysfsPath>/brightness (watched)
<sysfsPath>/max_brightness (unwatched)
```

For example:

```text
/sys/class/backlight/intel_backlight/brightness
/sys/class/backlight/intel_backlight/max_brightness
```

The current file reloads on change:

```qml
onFileChanged: {
    reload()
}
```

and pushes its content through:

```qml
ownerDevice.updateCurrentValue()
```

The max file pushes through:

```qml
ownerDevice.updateMaxValue()
```

only when it loads.

***

## 6.8 Integer parsing

`sysfs` content is text, so both updates go through:

```qml
Brightness.readInteger(value)
```

which performs:

```text
String(value).trim()
    ↓
parseInt(..., 10)
    ↓
non-finite -> 0
    ↓
max(0, result)
```

Negative or garbage content therefore becomes `0` rather than `NaN`.

***

## 6.9 Percent normalization

Each device computes:

```text
max > 0 ? clamp(value * 100 / max, 0, 100) : 0
```
