The service-level properties then forward the active device:

```text
device.percent -> Brightness.percent
round          -> percentRounded
String + "%"  -> percentText
```

When there is no active device, or `max <= 0`:

```text
percent = 0
percentText = "0%"
```

***

## 6.10 Default and active device

The default is:

```qml
Brightness.findDefaultDevice()
```

which performs:

```text
first isBacklight -> return it
otherwise         -> return _devices[0]
otherwise         -> null
```

The active device is:

```qml
Brightness.device
```

which performs:

```text
_selectedKey non-empty
    ↓
deviceForKey(_selectedKey) or defaultDevice
otherwise
    ↓
defaultDevice
```

All service-level `value`, `max`, `percent`, `deviceName`, and `deviceKey` bindings follow this one property.

***

## 6.11 Device lookup

`deviceForKey()` is the single lookup primitive:

```text
undefined / null / "" -> null
otherwise              -> linear scan by key
```

`deviceFor()` only builds the key:

```qml
Brightness.deviceFor(
    className,
    deviceId
)
```

becomes conceptually:

```text
deviceForKey(className + ":" + deviceId)
```

`resolveDevice()` adds polymorphism:

```text
null / undefined            -> null
object with usable key      -> deviceForKey(object.key)
object without usable key   -> null
string                      -> deviceForKey(String(value))
```

A removed device resolves to `null`, so stale object references fail safely instead of addressing the wrong hardware.

***

## 6.12 `set()` semantics

`set()` is the single absolute-write primitive.

It performs:

```text
resolveDevice(device)
    ↓
missing -> false
    ↓
Number(value)
    ↓
non-finite -> false
    ↓
clamp 0 -> 100
    ↓
runOperation(target, "<percent>%")
```

For example:

```qml
Brightness.set(device, 70)
```

runs conceptually:

```text
brightnessctl --quiet --class backlight --device intel_backlight set 70%
```

and returns `true` when that process starts.

***

## 6.13 `increase()` and `decrease()` semantics

Both are relative-write primitives.

They perform:

```text
resolveDevice(device)
    ↓
missing -> false
    ↓
Number(amount)
    ↓
non-finite or <= 0 -> step = 5
    ↓
runOperation(target, "+<step>%")
runOperation(target, "-<step>%")
```

For example:

```qml
Brightness.increase(device, 5)
```

runs conceptually:

```text
brightnessctl set +5%
```

The `5` default keeps brightness keys and scroll handlers working when the caller omits the step.

***

## 6.14 Control process lifecycle

Each operation creates its own `Process`:

```text
runOperation()
    ↓
createObject(controlProcessComponent)
    ↓
failed -> warn + false
    ↓
process.running = true
    ↓
return true
```

On exit:

```text
non-zero + target -> warn with key + exit code
target exists     -> target.refresh()
destroy process
```

The refresh reloads both `FileView` objects when loaded, so QML state converges without polling.

***

## 6.15 Selection lifecycle

Selecting performs:

```text
Brightness.setDevice(key)
    ↓
deviceForKey(key)
    ↓
missing -> false, selection unchanged
    ↓
_selectedKey = target.key
    ↓
return true
```

Resetting performs:

```text
Brightness.resetDevice()
    ↓
_selectedKey = ""
    ↓
return true
```

The complete active-device lifecycle is therefore:

```text
discovery commits _devices
        │
        ▼
defaultDevice reevaluates
        │
        ▼
device reevaluates (selected or default)
        │
        ▼
value / max / percent bindings reevaluate
```

***

## 6.16 `deviceInfo()` serialization

`deviceInfo()` converts one live device into plain JSON-safe data:

```json
{
    "key": "backlight:intel_backlight",
    "id": "intel_backlight",
    "class": "backlight",
    "name": "intel_backlight",
    "displayName": "intel_backlight",
    "type": "backlight",
    "isBacklight": true,
    "isLed": false,
    "isPresent": true,
    "value": 1200,
    "max": 4800,
    "percent": 25,
    "percentText": "25%",
    "sysfsPath": "/sys/class/backlight/intel_backlight",
    "selected": true
}
```

`selected` compares object identity:

```qml
root.device === device
```

When the argument is null, the function returns:

```json
{}
```

***

## 6.17 IPC architecture

IPC is a thin external interface over the same service API.

Conceptually:

```text
terminal
   │
   ▼
n0ctos-brightness
   │
   ▼
Brightness.qml
   │
   ▼
brightnessctl / sysfs
```

For example:

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-brightness set 70
```

becomes conceptually:

```qml
Brightness.set(
    Brightness.device,
    70
)
```

and:

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-brightness list
```

becomes conceptually:

```qml
JSON.stringify(
    Brightness.devices.map(Brightness.deviceInfo)
)
```

The IPC layer serializes values as strings and booleans for terminal use.

***

## 6.18 No polling

Brightness does not use a polling timer to detect changes.

There is no:

```qml
Timer {
    interval: 1000
    repeat: true

    onTriggered:
        reloadBrightness()
}
```

Changes arrive through:

```text
FileView fileChanged -> reload -> update value
control exit        -> device.refresh()
discovery exit      -> applyDiscovery()
```

This avoids unnecessary CPU activity.

***

## 6.19 Service boundaries

The responsibilities are intentionally divided:

```text
Brightness
    device discovery parsing
    device objects and selection
    percent normalization
    control operations
    device info API

brightnessctl
    hardware enumeration
    actual brightness changes

sysfs FileView
    current and maximum value tracking
    external change notification
```

Brightness should not reimplement hardware enumeration or bypass `brightnessctl` with direct `sysfs` writes.

***

## 6.20 What UI / service code should not do

Components should not:

```text
spawn brightnessctl directly

create FileView objects for brightness files

parse brightnessctl --list output

assume one fixed backlight name

assume devices never change

mutate Brightness.devices in place

send foreign objects to set/increase/decrease
```

Instead:

```qml
Brightness.percentText
Brightness.device
Brightness.set(...)
Brightness.increase(...)
Brightness.decrease(...)
Brightness.setDevice(...)
```

should be the normal interface.

***

## 6.21 Final architecture summary

The entire system can be viewed as:

```text
                         Component
                            │
                            │ property binding / set()
                            ▼
                    ┌─────────────────┐
                    │   Brightness    │
                    │                 │
                    │ discovery       │
                    │ devices         │
                    │ active device   │
                    │ percent         │
                    │ control         │
                    └────────┬────────┘
                             │
                             │ brightnessctl + sysfs API
                             ▼
                    ┌─────────────────┐
                    │ brightnessctl / │
                    │     sysfs       │
                    │                 │
                    │ device list     │
                    │ brightness file │
                    │ max file        │
                    │ set operation   │
                    └────────┬────────┘
                             │
                             ▼
                    backlight + LED hardware
```

The core rule is:

> **Components read what brightness they need; `Brightness.qml` decides which device it comes from and how percent is normalized; `brightnessctl` and `sysfs` handle how hardware state is enumerated and changed.**


# Clipboard Service



`Clipboard.qml` is N0ctOS's centralized Wayland clipboard history service.

It gives every shell component one consistent place to read clipboard history, restore entries, and configure retention without touching the filesystem or `wl-clipboard` directly.

The service supports automatic capture via `wl-paste --watch`, file-backed history, per-entry MIME kinds, bounded retention, reactive history-size configuration, and restore via `wl-copy`.

The normal usage pattern is:

```text
Wayland clipboard
    │
    ▼
Clipboard watcher (wl-paste --watch)
    │
    ▼
Clipboard
    │
    ├── items (newest first)
    ├── current (items[0])
    └── historySize
    │
    ├── items/ + history.json
    └── Config (historySize only)
```

***

# 1. What does it do?

`Clipboard.qml` captures every Wayland clipboard change and keeps a bounded, persistent history.

A history entry looks like this:

```json
{
    "id": "1759000000000-3",
    "path": "/home/user/.local/share/N0ctOS/clipboard/items/entry-AbCdEfGh",
    "mime": "text/plain;charset=utf-8",
    "kind": "text",
    "size": 42,
    "timestamp": 1759000000000
}
```

The entry bytes live in a separate file under `items/`. `history.json` stores only this metadata array, newest first:

```json
[
    {
        "id": "1759000000000-3",
        "path": ".../items/entry-AbCdEfGh",
        "mime": "text/plain;charset=utf-8",
        "kind": "text",
        "size": 42,
        "timestamp": 1759000000000
    },
    {
        "id": "1759000000000-2",
        "path": ".../items/entry-XyZ12345",
        "mime": "image/png",
        "kind": "image",
        "size": 18344,
        "timestamp": 1758999990000
    }
]
```

Retention is configured through `Config`:

```json
{
    "clipboard": {
        "historySize": 50
    }
}
```

The effective history order is always:

```text
index 0 = newest (current)
    ↓
index 1 = previous
    ↓
index N = oldest (trimmed beyond historySize)
```

So a component can simply do:

```qml
Clipboard.current
```

or restore an older entry with:

```qml
Clipboard.copy(2)
```

and not care where the bytes are stored, what MIME type they use, or how retention works.

If `wl-clipboard` is missing, the service reports `available === false` and **never starts the watcher**.

***

# 2. UI API

Import normally:

```qml
import QtQuick
import Quickshell

import qs.services
```

## Core API

| How to call                             | What does it do                                                                                   |
| --------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Clipboard.items`                       | History array, newest first. Read-only view of `_history`.                                        |
| `Clipboard.count`                       | Number of history entries.                                                                        |
| `Clipboard.current`                     | Newest entry (`items[0]`), or `null` when empty.                                                  |
| `Clipboard.available`                   | `true` when `wl-paste` and `wl-copy` were found.                                                  |
| `Clipboard.watching`                    | `true` when the `wl-paste --watch` process is running.                                            |
| `Clipboard.historySize`                 | Normalized retention limit (1..500, default 50) from `Config`.                                    |
| `Clipboard.copy(index)`                 | Restores `items[index]` to the live clipboard via `wl-copy`. Returns `bool`.                      |
| `Clipboard.copyFile(path, mime)`        | Restores an arbitrary stored file with an explicit MIME type. Returns `bool`.                     |
| `Clipboard.copyText(value)`             | Copies a string as `text/plain`. Returns `bool`.                                                  |
| `Clipboard.remove(index)`               | Deletes one entry, removes its file, emits `itemRemoved`. Returns `bool`.                         |
| `Clipboard.clear()`                     | Deletes all entries and their files, emits `historyCleared`. Returns `bool`.                      |
| `Clipboard.trimHistory()`               | Drops entries beyond `historySize`, deleting their files. No-op before history is loaded.         |
| `Clipboard.scheduleHistorySave()`       | Marks history dirty and debounces a `history.json` write (50 ms). No-op before history is loaded. |
| `Clipboard.normalizeHistorySize(value)` | Normalizes any value to `1..500` (`NaN` → `50`, floored, clamped).                                |
| `Clipboard.setHistorySize(value)`       | Normalizes `value` and writes it via `Config.set("clipboard.historySize", …)`. Returns `bool`.    |

| Example                                             | Result                                                  |
| --------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Clipboard.copy(0)`                                 | `true`, `items[0]` restored to the live clipboard       |
| `Clipboard.copyFile("/path/to/entry", "image/png")` | `true`, file restored with MIME `image/png`             |
| `Clipboard.copyText("hello")`                       | `true`, `"hello"` on the live clipboard as `text/plain` |
| `Clipboard.remove(2)`                               | `true`, entry and its `items/entry-*` file deleted      |
| `Clipboard.setHistorySize(100)`                     | `true`, `historySize` becomes `100`                     |

Signals:

| Signal                            | When it fires                                                           |
| --------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `itemAdded(item)`                 | A new clipboard capture was prepended to `items`.                       |
| `itemRemoved(item)`               | One entry was removed by `remove()` or `trimHistory()`.                 |
| `historyCleared()`                | All entries were removed by `clear()`.                                  |
| `availabilityChangedExternally()` | Declared on the singleton; never emitted by the current implementation. |

Storage paths (read-only):

| Property                | Value                                                  |
| ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `Clipboard.homeDir`     | `$HOME`.                                               |
| `Clipboard.dataBase`    | `$XDG_DATA_HOME`, or `$HOME/.local/share` as fallback. |
| `Clipboard.dataDir`     | `<dataBase>/N0ctOS/clipboard`.                         |
| `Clipboard.itemsDir`    | `<dataDir>/items`.                                     |
| `Clipboard.historyPath` | `<dataDir>/history.json`.                              |

## History model

History is an index-addressed array, newest first.

| Concept        | Meaning                                              |
| -------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `index 0`      | Newest entry. Same object as `Clipboard.current`.    |
| `index N`      | Older entries in capture order.                      |
| `out of range` | `copy()` / `remove()` return `false` and do nothing. |
| `empty`        | `count === 0`, `items` is `[]`, `current` is `null`. |

For example:

```qml
Clipboard.copy(0)
```

restores:

```text
items[0] → wl-copy → live Wayland clipboard
```

while:

```qml
Clipboard.remove(0)
```

deletes:

```text
items[0] + its items/entry-* file
```

## Entry kinds

The watcher classifies every capture into one `kind`:

| Kind     | Meaning                                      | Typical MIME                                      |
| -------- | -------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| `text`   | Plain or generic text.                       | `text/plain`, `text/*`                            |
| `image`  | Any `image/*` type offered by the clipboard. | `image/png`                                       |
| `files`  | File list copied from a file manager.        | `text/uri-list`                                   |
| `binary` | Fallback when no known type matched.         | First offered type, or `application/octet-stream` |

MIME selection priority inside the watch script is:

```text
text/uri-list
    ↓
x-special/gnome-copied-files
    ↓
first ^image/
    ↓
first ^text/plain
    ↓
first ^text/
    ↓
first offered type
    ↓
application/octet-stream
```

A file-manager copy therefore becomes `kind: "files"` even when the clipboard also offers text.

### Typical component usage

```qml
readonly property var latest:
    Clipboard.current

readonly property int entryCount:
    Clipboard.count

readonly property bool canPaste:
    Clipboard.available &&
    Clipboard.count > 0
```

That is the intended everyday usage.

Components normally should not need to know how the watcher, `items/` files, or `history.json` persistence work.

***

# 3. IPC API

IPC target:

```text
n0ctos-clipboard
```

## Core reads

| How to call | What does it do                                     |
| ----------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| `count`     | Returns the number of history entries.              |
| `list`      | Returns all entries as a JSON string.               |
| `current`   | Returns the newest entry as a JSON string, or `""`. |

| Example                                | Result                                              |
| -------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| `qs ipc call n0ctos-clipboard count`   | entry count, e.g. `3`                               |
| `qs ipc call n0ctos-clipboard list`    | JSON array of history entries (see below)           |
| `qs ipc call n0ctos-clipboard current` | JSON object of the newest entry, or `""` when empty |

`list` returns a JSON array:

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-clipboard list
```

`current` returns one JSON object, or an empty string when history is empty:

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-clipboard current
```

## Other operations

| How to call          | What does it do                                                        |
| -------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `copy <index>`       | Restores `items[index]` to the live clipboard. Returns `bool`.         |
| `remove <index>`     | Deletes one entry and its file. Returns `bool`.                        |
| `clear`              | Deletes all entries and their files. Returns `bool`.                   |
| `copyText <value>`   | Copies a string as `text/plain`. Returns `bool`.                       |
| `watching`           | Returns whether the `wl-paste --watch` process is running.             |
| `historySize`        | Returns the normalized retention limit.                                |
| `setHistorySize <n>` | Normalizes `n` to `1..500` and stores it via `Config`. Returns `bool`. |

| Example                                           | Result                                           |
| ------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| `qs ipc call n0ctos-clipboard copy 0`             | `true`, `items[0]` restored                      |
| `qs ipc call n0ctos-clipboard remove 2`           | `true`, entry 2 deleted                          |
| `qs ipc call n0ctos-clipboard clear`              | `true`, all entries deleted                      |
| `qs ipc call n0ctos-clipboard copyText hello`     | `true`, `"hello"` copied as `text/plain`         |
| `qs ipc call n0ctos-clipboard watching`           | `true` while the `wl-paste --watch` process runs |
| `qs ipc call n0ctos-clipboard historySize`        | retention limit, e.g. `50`                       |
| `qs ipc call n0ctos-clipboard setHistorySize 100` | `true`, retention limit becomes `100`            |

Index arguments are integers:

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-clipboard copy 0
```

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-clipboard remove 2
```

Text:

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-clipboard copyText \
    "hello from the terminal"
```

Retention:

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-clipboard setHistorySize 100
```

Values outside `1..500` are clamped, not rejected. `NaN` becomes `50`.

***

# 4. Features / limitations

## Features

### Automatic Wayland capture

The service spawns one long-lived process:

```text
wl-paste --watch sh -c <watchScript>
```

Every clipboard change produces one watch record:

```text
path <TAB> mime <TAB> kind <TAB> size
```

The service parses that line, validates it, and prepends a history entry. No polling is involved.

### File-backed entry bytes

Clipboard bytes are never embedded in `history.json`.

Instead:

```text
items/entry-XXXXXXXX  ← raw bytes
history.json          ← metadata array
```

This keeps the JSON small and allows images and file lists to share the same history mechanism.

### MIME-aware kinds

Each entry records both the selected MIME type and a coarse `kind`:

```json
{
    "mime": "image/png",
    "kind": "image"
}
```

UI code can switch on `kind` without parsing MIME strings:

```qml
visible: modelData.kind === "image"
```

### Bounded history

`historySize` bounds the array:

```text
entries beyond historySize
        ↓
popped + file deleted + itemRemoved emitted
```

Trimming runs after every capture, after every `Config` revision change, and after every `historySize` change.

### Persistent history

History survives shell restarts:

```text
capture → _history → history.json → reload on next launch
```

Writes are debounced (50 ms), atomic, and guarded against overlapping saves and self-triggered reloads.

### Reactive retention

`historySize` is read from `Config`:

```qml
Config.get(
    "clipboard.historySize",
    50
)
```

Changing it anywhere (UI, IPC, external config edit) re-trims history and re-saves.

### Watcher self-healing

If the watcher exits while dependencies and storage are healthy, it restarts after 1500 ms.

```text
watcher exits
    ↓
warn + 1500 ms timer
    ↓
start again when ready
```

### Restore without exposing internals

Consumers never invoke `wl-copy` themselves:

```qml
Clipboard.copy(0)
Clipboard.copyText("hello")
```

The service builds the correct `wl-copy --type <mime>` command internally.

***

## Limitations

### `wl-clipboard` is required

Both binaries must exist:

```text
wl-paste
wl-copy
```

If either is missing, the service logs an install hint, sets `available` to `false`, and never starts the watcher:

```bash
sudo pacman -S wl-clipboard
```

History from a previous session is still loaded, but no new captures occur.

### History stores paths, not inline text

`list` and `items` return metadata with a `path` field.

To read the actual text, the consumer must read that file:

```text
items[i].path → file bytes
```

There is no `getText(index)` helper in the current implementation.

### Index-based access shifts

Entries are addressed by position:

```qml
Clipboard.copy(0)
Clipboard.remove(2)
```

A new capture prepends at index `0` and shifts every existing index by one. Holding an index across captures is therefore unsafe; hold the entry `id` instead.

### Restoring re-captures

`copy()` and `copyText()` place data on the live Wayland clipboard, which the watcher observes like any other change.

Expect:

```text
copy(2)
    ↓
same bytes re-captured as new items[0]
```

This is inherent to a `wl-paste --watch` design, not a bug.

### No deduplication

Consecutive copies of identical content create separate entries with distinct `id` values.

The service never compares bytes or skips a capture.

### No per-kind or per-size filtering

Every accepted watch record enters history, whether it is:

```text
12 bytes of text
a 40 MB image
a file list
```

Only `historySize` bounds growth. There is no maximum-bytes or kind-exclusion setting.

### `availabilityChangedExternally` is currently unused

The signal is declared:

```qml
signal availabilityChangedExternally()
```

but nothing in the current implementation emits it. Availability changes are observable through the `available` property instead.

***

# 5. Example use cases

## 5.1 Showing history in a list

Bind directly to the reactive history array:

```qml
import QtQuick
import Quickshell

import qs.services

ListView {
    model: Clipboard.items

    delegate: Text {
        required property var modelData
        required property int index

        text: "#" + index + " " + modelData.kind + " (" + modelData.size + " B)"
    }
}
```

New captures, removals, and clears update the view automatically because `items` is a reactive alias of the internal history.

An empty state can use:

```qml
visible: Clipboard.count === 0
```

***

## 5.2 Restoring an entry on click

The newest entry is index `0`:

```qml
MouseArea {
    anchors.fill: parent

    onClicked: Clipboard.copy(0)
}
```

An older entry uses its delegate index:

```qml
delegate: MouseArea {
    required property int index

    anchors.fill: parent

    onClicked: Clipboard.copy(index)
}
```

Out-of-range indices safely return `false`.

***

## 5.3 Copying new text from the UI

A text field can push text without touching `wl-copy`:

```qml
Row {
    spacing: 8

    TextInput {
        id: input
        width: 200
    }

    Rectangle {
        width: 80
        height: 32

        MouseArea {
            anchors.fill: parent

            onClicked: Clipboard.copyText(input.text)
        }
    }
}
```

The new text appears on the live clipboard and is then re-captured as the newest history entry.

***

## 5.4 Removing one entry or clearing all

Remove a single row:

```qml
Clipboard.remove(2)
```

Clear everything:

```qml
Clipboard.clear()
```

The backing `items/entry-*` files are deleted with `rm -f` in the background, and the UI updates through:

```text
remove → itemRemoved
clear  → historyCleared
```

***

## 5.5 Configuring retention from the UI

Read the normalized limit:

```qml
Text {
    text: "Keep " + Clipboard.historySize + " entries"
}
```

Write a new limit:

```qml
Clipboard.setHistorySize(100)
```

The value is clamped to `1..500`, persisted through `Config`, and immediately trims history if it shrank.

***

## 5.6 Reacting to captures and removals

Connect to the history signals:

```qml
Connections {
    target: Clipboard

    function onItemAdded(item) {
        console.log("captured", item.kind, item.size)
    }

    function onItemRemoved(item) {
        console.log("removed", item.id)
    }

    function onHistoryCleared() {
        console.log("history cleared")
    }
}
```

This is the right place for toasts, badges, or refreshing a popover.

***

## 5.7 Terminal workflow

List everything:

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-clipboard list
```

Show the newest entry:

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-clipboard current
```

Restore the newest entry:

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-clipboard copy 0
```

Push text from the terminal:

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-clipboard copyText \
    "deploy at 18:00"
```

Delete one entry:

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-clipboard remove 2
```

Clear all history:

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-clipboard clear
```

Check watcher health and retention:

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-clipboard watching
qs ipc call n0ctos-clipboard historySize
qs ipc call n0ctos-clipboard setHistorySize 100
```

***

# 6. Detailed architecture

This section is for developers working on `Clipboard.qml` and the services/components that consume it.

***

## 6.1 Overall architecture

The service sits between Wayland, the filesystem, and `Config`:

```text
Wayland clipboard
        │
        ▼
wl-paste --watch + watchScript
        │
        ▼
  Clipboard.qml
        │
   ┌────┼─────────┐
   │    │         │
   ▼    ▼         ▼
 items/ history  Config
 files  .json    (historySize)
```

There are effectively three responsibilities:

```text
wl-clipboard
    live clipboard capture and restore

Clipboard.qml
    history capture, retention, restore API

Config + history.json
    small-setting persistence + history persistence
```

Clipboard should not duplicate the file-watching and write-queue logic already provided by `Config` and `FileView`.

***

## 6.2 Storage layout

Paths derive from the environment:

```text
$XDG_DATA_HOME (or $HOME/.local/share)
        │
        ▼
N0ctOS/clipboard/
        │
        ├── items/
        │     └── entry-XXXXXXXX (raw bytes)
        │
        └── history.json (metadata array)
```

Concretely:

```qml
readonly property string dataDir: root.dataBase + "/N0ctOS/clipboard"
readonly property string itemsDir: root.dataDir + "/items"
readonly property string historyPath: root.dataDir + "/history.json"
```

The directory is created once at startup with `mkdir -p`.

***

## 6.3 History entry shape

Every entry has the same six fields:

```json
{
    "id": "<Date.now>-<sequence>",
    "path": "<itemsDir>/entry-XXXXXXXX",
    "mime": "text/plain;charset=utf-8",
    "kind": "text",
    "size": 42,
    "timestamp": 1759000000000
}
```

Semantics:

```text
id         unique per capture (millis + monotonic sequence)
path       backing file inside itemsDir
mime       MIME type selected by the watch script
kind       text | image | files | binary
size       byte count, clamped to >= 0
timestamp  Date.now() at capture time
```

`id` ordering is capture order; array position is recency order.

***

## 6.4 Watch pipeline

One capture flows through four stages:

```text
wl-paste --watch fires
        │
        ▼
watchScript stores stdin → temp file
        │
        ▼
watchScript prints: path TAB mime TAB kind TAB size
        │
        ▼
SplitParser splits on \n → _handleWatchRecord(line)
        │
        ▼
validate → prepend → trim → itemAdded → save
```

The watcher process is declared as:

```text
wl-paste --watch sh -c <watchScript> n0ctos-clipboard <itemsDir>
```

`stdout` uses a `SplitParser` with `\n` as the split marker, so each record arrives as one trimmed line.

***

## 6.5 Watch-script MIME selection

The script stores bytes first, then asks what types are offered:

```text
cat stdin → mktemp file
    ↓
wc -c → size
    ↓
wl-paste --list-types → selection
```

Selection priority is:

```text
1. text/uri-list → kind files
2. x-special/gnome-copied-files → kind files
3. first ^image/ → kind image
4. first ^text/plain(;…) → kind text
5. first ^text/ → kind text
6. first offered type → kind binary
7. empty → application/octet-stream → kind binary
```

The script never interprets file contents. It only ranks the offered type list.

***

## 6.6 Record validation

`_handleWatchRecord()` rejects anything unexpected:

```text
empty line → ignore
    ↓
fewer than 4 TAB fields → warn + ignore
    ↓
path outside itemsDir + "/" → warn + ignore
    ↓
otherwise → accept
```

The path-prefix check is a security boundary:

```text
allowed: <itemsDir>/entry-XXXXXXXX
rejected: /tmp/evil, /home/user/other, <itemsDir> itself
```

Only files the watch script just created inside `items/` can enter history.

***

## 6.7 Startup lifecycle

Startup has three parallel prerequisites:

```text
Component.onCompleted
    ├── mkdir -p itemsDir → _storageReady → reload history file
    └── check wl-paste + wl-copy → _available → maybe start watcher
```

History loading then decides:

```text
FileNotFound + storage ready
    → [] → save → watcher may start

parse error / corrupt JSON
    → log → [] → watcher may start (no overwrite)

valid array
    → keep entries with path + mime → trim → watcher may start
```

A corrupt file is deliberately not overwritten automatically, so a bad write cannot silently erase history on the next launch.

The watcher starts only when all of these hold:

```text
_available
_storageReady
_historyLoaded
not already started
```

***

## 6.8 History load filtering

Load keeps the file format forgiving:

```text
empty file → []
non-array root → invalid, reset to []
non-object row → skipped
object without path or mime → skipped
```

Surviving rows are kept verbatim, including any extra fields a future version might add. No migration step rewrites them.

***

## 6.9 Save lifecycle (debounced)

Saves are debounced through a 50 ms single-shot timer:

```text
capture / remove / clear / trim-request / config change
        │
        ▼
scheduleHistorySave() → _historyWritePending = true → restart timer
        │
        ▼ (50 ms quiet)
_writeHistory() → FileView.setText(JSON + "\n")
        │
        ▼
onSaved → _historySaving = false → flush pending if any
onSaveFailed → _historySaving = false → keep pending = true
```

Guards:

```text
not loaded → never schedule or write
already saving → skip; pending flag retries after onSaved
storage not ready → skip write
```

External edits are detected but self-writes are ignored:

```text
onFileChanged while _historySaving → ignore (own write)
otherwise → reload from disk
```

***

## 6.10 Trim semantics

`trimHistory()` enforces `historySize`:

```text
while history.length > limit
    pop oldest
        ↓
    rm -f its file (detached)
        ↓
    emit itemRemoved
```

Notes:

```text
no-op before history is loaded
files are deleted best-effort via execDetached
trim itself does not save; callers schedule the save
```

Trim is invoked from capture handling, `historySize` changes, and `Config.revision` changes.

***

## 6.11 Copy semantics

`copy(index)` is bounds-checked restoration:

```text
index < 0 or >= length → false
entry without path/mime → false
otherwise → copyFile(path, mime)
```

`copyFile(path, mime)` runs detached:

```text
sh -c 'exec wl-copy --type "$1" < "$2"' … <mime> <path>
```

`copyText(value)` runs detached:

```text
printf "%s" <value> | wl-copy --type text/plain
```

All three return `true` once the process is spawned, not once `wl-copy` completes. Failure of the detached process is not propagated back.

***

## 6.12 Remove and clear semantics

`remove(index)`:

```text
bounds check
    ↓
splice one row → assign new array (keeps bindings reactive)
    ↓
rm -f its file
    ↓
emit itemRemoved → schedule save → true
```

`clear()`:

```text
rm -f every entry file
    ↓
_history = []
    ↓
emit historyCleared → schedule save → true
```

Both keep the in-memory array as the source of truth; the file write follows asynchronously.

***

## 6.13 Config integration

Only one setting flows through `Config`:

```json
{
    "clipboard": {
        "historySize": 50
    }
}
```

Read path:

```qml
Config.get("clipboard.historySize", 50)
```

Write path:

```qml
Config.set("clipboard.historySize", normalized)
```

History bytes and `history.json` deliberately bypass `Config` and use a dedicated `FileView`, because they are a growing data store, not a small user setting.

***

## 6.14 Normalization

`normalizeHistorySize()` makes any input safe:

```text
Number(value)
    ↓
not finite → 50
    ↓
floor
    ↓
clamp 1..500
```

So:

```text
100 → 100
0 → 1
9999 → 500
"abc" → 50
12.9 → 12
```

IPC and UI callers share this one function, so both surfaces behave identically.

***

## 6.15 Reactive state

The service consumes the reactive `Config` document:

```text
config file changes
        │
        ▼
Config.revision changes
        │
        ▼
historySize reevaluates → trimHistory() → schedule save
        │
        ▼
component bindings (items / count / current) reevaluate
```

Consumers never reload manually:

```qml
readonly property int entryCount: Clipboard.count
```

reevaluates whenever the underlying `_history` array is reassigned.

***

## 6.16 Watcher supervision

The watcher is supervised, not fire-and-forget:

```text
started → _watchStarted = true + log
    ↓
exited → _watchStarted = false + warn
    ↓
available && storageReady → restart after 1500 ms
```

A restart storm is avoided by the single-shot 1500 ms timer and the `_startWatcherIfReady()` guard, which refuses to start twice.

***

## 6.17 IPC architecture

IPC is a thin external interface over the same service API.

Conceptually:

```text
terminal
   │
   ▼
n0ctos-clipboard
   │
   ▼
Clipboard.qml
   │
   ├── items/ + history.json
   └── Config (historySize)
```

For example:

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-clipboard copy 0
```

becomes conceptually:

```qml
Clipboard.copy(0)
```

The IPC layer serializes history as JSON strings because `qs ipc` transports strings most conveniently.

***

## 6.18 Performance model

Normal UI operation is cheap:

```text
QML binding
    ↓
Clipboard
    ↓
in-memory array lookup
```

There is no filesystem read per binding evaluation. Filesystem work happens only on:

```text
watcher capture (one small file + one debounced JSON write)
copy / remove / clear (one detached process per file)
startup load (one JSON parse)
```

`history.json` is pretty-printed with 2-space indent plus a trailing newline, so external inspection stays readable without affecting runtime cost.

***

## 6.19 What UI / service code should not do

Components should not:

```text
invoke wl-paste / wl-copy directly

create FileView objects for clipboard history

read or write items/ or history.json directly

implement clipboard polling timers

cache Clipboard.items and assume indices stay valid

mutate Clipboard.items array elements in place

assume availabilityChangedExternally() will fire
```

Instead:

```qml
Clipboard.items
Clipboard.current
Clipboard.copy(...)
Clipboard.copyText(...)
Clipboard.remove(...)
Clipboard.clear(...)
Clipboard.setHistorySize(...)
```

should be the normal interface.

***

## 6.20 Final architecture summary

The entire system can be viewed as:

```text
                     Wayland clipboard
                             │
                    capture / restore
                             │
                     ┌─────────────────┐
                     │    Clipboard    │
                     │                 │
                     │ items (newest   │
                     │   first)        │
                     │ current         │
                     │ historySize     │
                     │ watcher         │
                     │ trim + save     │
                     └────────┬────────┘
                              │
              ┌───────────────┼───────────────┐
              │               │               │
              ▼               ▼               ▼
       ┌────────────┐  ┌────────────┐  ┌────────────┐
       │   items/   │  │ history    │  │   Config   │
       │            │  │  .json     │  │            │
       │ raw bytes  │  │ metadata   │  │ historySize│
       │ per entry  │  │ array      │  │ only       │
       └────────────┘  └────────────┘  └────────────┘
```

The core rule is:

> **Wayland owns the live clipboard; `Clipboard.qml` owns capture, history, and restore; `history.json` + `items/` own persistence; `Config` owns only `clipboard.historySize`.**


# Config Service



`Config.qml` is N0ctOS's centralized configuration interface.

`ConfigStore.qml` is the underlying configuration engine responsible for loading, tracking, modifying, saving, watching, and managing configuration files. It stays covered inside this document; there is no separate file.

It gives every shell component and service one consistent place to read and write JSON configuration without touching files directly, creating `FileView` objects, or implementing persistence logic.

The service supports multiple registered configuration files, reactive documents, per-file state, autosave-everything with explicit `save()` checkpoints, delta-based undo/redo/revert history, file watching with debounced reloads, atomic writes with a save queue, a path registry with CRUD, and a high-level IPC interface.

The normal usage pattern is:

```text
Component / Service
    │
    ▼
Config
    │
    ├── reactive documents
    ├── per-file state
    └── path registry
    │
    ▼
ConfigStore
    │
    ▼
JSON configuration files
```

***

# 1. What does it do?

`Config.qml` sits between N0ctOS services/UI and configuration files.

A service can read:

```qml
Config.get(
    "notifications.isDnd",
    false
)
```

or write:

```qml
Config.set(
    "notifications.isDnd",
    true
)
```

A configuration document can contain simple values:

```json
{
    "notifications": {
        "isDnd": true
    }
}
```

or nested sections:

```json
{
    "notifications": {
        "popup": {
            "timeout": {
                "normal": 5
            }
        }
    }
}
```

A secondary file can be selected with a file key:

```json
{
    "wifi": {
        "enabled": true
    }
}
```

read as:

```qml
Config.get(
    "wifi.enabled",
    true,
    "networkConfig"
)
```

The effective file is resolved in this order:

```text
requested fileKey
    ↓
registered?
    ↓
yes -> requested file
no  -> homeConfig
```

So a component can simply do:

```qml
Config.get(
    "audio.volume",
    100
)
```

and not care where the file lives, how it is watched, or how it is written.

If that property does not exist, the fallback is returned.

If an unknown file key is supplied to a normal configuration operation, `homeConfig` is used instead:

```qml
Config.get(
    "some.value",
    false,
    "doesNotExist"
)
```

resolves to:

```text
~/.config/N0ctOS/config.json
```

Path-registry operations are different. They use exact key matching and do not fall back:

```qml
Config.hasPath(
    "doesNotExist"
)
```

returns `false` instead of operating on `homeConfig`.

***

# 2. UI API

Import normally:

```qml
import QtQuick
import Quickshell

import qs.services
```

## Core API

| How to read             | What does it do                                                                                                                       |
| ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Config.data`           | Current document of the default file (`homeConfig`). Equivalent to `documentFor("homeConfig")`. Reactive.                             |
| `Config.documents`      | Currently loaded documents indexed by file key. Reactive.                                                                             |
| `Config.isReady`        | `true` when the default document has been loaded and initialized.                                                                     |
| `Config.isWriting`      | `true` while the default file has a write pipeline active (`writing`/`writePending`/queued text).                                     |
| `Config.isDirty`        | `true` when the default document differs from its last `save()`/load baseline. Autosave already wrote the file; `save()` clears this. |
| `Config.revision`       | Revision number of the default document. Increases when the in-memory document changes.                                               |
| `Config.configPath`     | Resolved physical path of `homeConfig`, e.g. `/home/user/.config/N0ctOS/config.json`.                                                 |
| `Config.paths`          | Registered file-key table (`key -> resolved physical path`). Reactive.                                                                |
| `Config.pathKeys`       | List of registered configuration keys. Reactive.                                                                                      |
| `Config.defaultFileKey` | Default file key (`"homeConfig"`).                                                                                                    |
| `Config.isDebugLogging` | Read-only mirror of `ConfigStore.isDebugLogging`. Set via `ConfigStore.isDebugLogging`.                                               |

## Reads

| How to call                                    | What does it do                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ---------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Config.get(dataPath, fallbackValue, fileKey)` | Reads a value at a dotted data path. Returns `fallbackValue` when missing. Unknown `fileKey` warns once, then falls back to `homeConfig`.                                                                                                                                                    |
| `Config.has(dataPath, fileKey)`                | Checks whether a property exists. Returns `true` when it exists, `false` when it does not. Unknown `fileKey` warns once, then falls back to `homeConfig`.                                                                                                                                    |
| `Config.documentFor(fileKey)`                  | Returns a snapshot clone of the complete document for a file key. Mutating the returned object never affects the store; use `set()`/`update()`/`remove()`/`undo()`/`redo()`/`revert()`. Unknown `fileKey` warns once, then falls back to `homeConfig`. Returns `{}` when no document exists. |
| `Config.isReadyFor(fileKey)`                   | `true` when the given file is ready. Unknown `fileKey` falls back to `homeConfig`.                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `Config.isWritingFor(fileKey)`                 | `true` while the given file has a write pipeline active. Unknown `fileKey` falls back to `homeConfig`.                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `Config.isDirtyFor(fileKey)`                   | `true` when the given file differs from its baseline. Unknown `fileKey` falls back to `homeConfig`.                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `Config.revisionFor(fileKey)`                  | Revision number for the given file, `0` when unknown. Unknown `fileKey` falls back to `homeConfig`.                                                                                                                                                                                          |

| Example                                             | Result                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| --------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Config.get("notifications.isDnd", false)`          | Stored value, or `false` when missing                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `Config.get("wifi.enabled", true, "networkConfig")` | Stored value from `networkConfig`, or `true` when missing; `homeConfig` value when key is unknown                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `Config.has("notifications.isDnd")`                 | `true` when the property exists, `false` when it does not                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `Config.has("wifi.enabled", "networkConfig")`       | `true` when the property exists in `networkConfig`, `false` when it does not                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `Config.documentFor("networkConfig")`               | Full document snapshot for `networkConfig` (`homeConfig` document when key is unknown). Read-only: mutate via `set()`/`update()`/`remove()`, never by editing the returned object                                                                                                  |
| `Config.historyAt("networkConfig")`                 | `{past:[...], future:[...], canUndo, canRedo, count, limit, isDirty}` for `networkConfig`. Each entry is `{op, dataPath, changeCount, changes:[{path, beforeExists, beforeValue, afterExists, afterValue}]}`. `future[0]` is the next redo. Unknown key falls back to `homeConfig` |
| `Config.historyFor("networkConfig")`                | Alias of `historyAt()`. Kept for convenience                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `Config.isReadyFor("networkConfig")`                | `true` when ready, `false` otherwise                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `Config.isWritingFor("networkConfig")`              | `true` while writing, `false` otherwise                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `Config.isDirtyFor("networkConfig")`                | `true` when unsaved changes exist, `false` otherwise                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `Config.revisionFor("networkConfig")`               | Revision number, `0` when no state exists                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |

## Writes

| How to call                               | What does it do                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| ----------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Config.set(dataPath, value, fileKey)`    | Creates or updates one value. Missing intermediate objects are created automatically. Autosaves immediately (memory + disk write queued). No-op (`true`, no write, no revision) when already equal. Rejects empty paths and `undefined` values. Unknown `fileKey` warns once, then falls back to `homeConfig`. |
| `Config.update(dataPath, value, fileKey)` | Deep-merges an object value into a data path, then persists through the normal autosave path. Requires a non-empty path and an object value. Unknown `fileKey` warns once, then falls back to `homeConfig`.                                                                                                    |
| `Config.remove(dataPath, fileKey)`        | Deletes a nested property and autosaves. Returns `false` and changes nothing when the path does not exist. Unknown `fileKey` warns once, then falls back to `homeConfig`.                                                                                                                                      |

| Example                                                     | Result                                                                                                                                               |
| ----------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Config.set("notifications.isDnd", true)`                   | `true` and document changed plus autosave write queued; `true` with no write/revision when already equal; `false` on empty path or `undefined` value |
| `Config.set("wifi.enabled", false, "networkConfig")`        | `true` and `networkConfig` document changed plus autosave write queued (`homeConfig` when key is unknown); `false` when rejected                     |
| `Config.update("notifications", {"isDnd": true})`           | `true` and value deep-merged plus autosave write queued; `false` when path is empty or value is not an object                                        |
| `Config.update("wifi", {"enabled": true}, "networkConfig")` | `true` and `networkConfig` value deep-merged plus autosave write queued; `false` when rejected                                                       |
| `Config.remove("notifications.isDnd")`                      | `true` and property deleted plus autosave write queued; `false` when the path does not exist                                                         |
| `Config.remove("wifi.enabled", "networkConfig")`            | `true` and property deleted from `networkConfig` plus autosave write queued; `false` when the path does not exist                                    |

## Undo history

Model: **autosave everything + explicit checkpoint**. Every `set()`/`update()`/`remove()`/`undo()`/`redo()`/`revert()` updates memory *and* immediately queues a disk write. `isDirty` means "document differs from the last `save()`/load baseline", not "disk differs" — after autosave the file already matches memory, but the file stays dirty until `save()` establishes a new baseline and wipes history.

Each mutation records one compact forward-delta entry (`past`), up to `historyLimit` (100) entries for `past + future` combined. When over the limit the oldest `past` entry is discarded first so redo is preserved. A new mutation clears `future` (kills redo). `save()` and `revert()` wipe both stacks.

| How to call              | What does it do                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| ------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Config.undo(fileKey)`   | Moves the newest `past` entry to `future`, restores its before-values, autosaves. Returns `false` when `past` is empty or the file is not ready. A no-op undo (entry resolves to the current document) still advances the stack but skips write/revision. Any undo cancels a pending `save()` checkpoint. Defaults to `homeConfig`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `Config.redo(fileKey)`   | Moves the newest `future` entry back to `past`, restores its after-values, autosaves. Returns `false` when `future` is empty or the file is not ready. No-op redos advance the stack without write/revision. A new `set()`/`update()`/`remove()` clears `future`. Defaults to `homeConfig`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `Config.revert(fileKey)` | Logically `while (canUndo) undo()`: replays every `past` before-value in reverse to restore the clean baseline, coalesced into a **single** document commit (single write, single revision, single `documentChanged`). Then wipes `past + future`. Returns `false` when not ready, or when `past` is empty *and* already clean. Undone-to-clean with redo available wipes without disk IO. Defaults to `homeConfig`.                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `Config.save(fileKey)`   | True checkpoint. Fails (`false`) when not ready. Clean + empty history: `true` no-op, no IO. Clean with leftover history (e.g. undo-to-clean leaves redo): wipes history, `true`, no IO, no revision. Dirty + write pipeline active: marks checkpoint-when-idle and ensures the newest state is queued; baseline/history reset in `onSaved`. Dirty + idle + last write failed: forces a rewrite, checkpoint on `onSaved`. Dirty + idle + disk already matches (normal autosave case): sets baseline + wipes history synchronously, `true`, no IO (avoids a same-content write that would never complete). |

| IPC                                                                          | Result                                                                                                                           |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `qs ipc call n0ctos-config undo` / `redo` / `revert`                         | `"true"` on success; `"false"` when there is nothing to undo/redo, when `revert` is already clean, or when the file is not ready |
| `qs ipc call n0ctos-config undoAt networkConfig` (same `redoAt`, `revertAt`) | Per-file variants                                                                                                                |

## File control

| How to call              | What does it do                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `Config.save(fileKey)`   | True checkpoint (see Undo history). Defaults to `homeConfig`. Normal `set()`/`update()`/`remove()` already autosave; `save()` only moves the baseline and wipes history.                   |
| `Config.reload(fileKey)` | Explicitly reloads one file from disk. Discards unsaved local state for that file (baseline = disk, history wiped). Defaults to `homeConfig`. Rejected while the write pipeline is active. |
| `Config.reloadAll()`     | Reloads every registered file. Skips files currently being written.                                                                                                                        |

| Example                          | Result                                                                                                                                                |
| -------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Config.save()`                  | `true` checkpoint for `homeConfig` (sync when idle, deferred to `onSaved` while writes are in flight); `false` when no controller exists or not ready |
| `Config.save("networkConfig")`   | `true` checkpoint for `networkConfig`; `false` when no controller exists or not ready                                                                 |
| `Config.reload()`                | `true` and `homeConfig` reloaded (local dirty state discarded); `false` while writing or when no controller exists                                    |
| `Config.reload("networkConfig")` | `true` and `networkConfig` reloaded (local dirty state discarded); `false` while writing or when no controller exists                                 |
| `Config.reloadAll()`             | `true` when every file reloaded; `false` when one or more files were skipped or failed                                                                |

## Path registry

| How to call                            | What does it do                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `Config.registerPath(fileKey, fsPath)` | Registers one logical file key. Same key plus same path is idempotent. Rejects empty keys/paths, same key with a different path, and duplicate physical paths.                                                           |
| `Config.registerPaths(pathTable)`      | Registers multiple files at once. Requires an object. Returns `false` when one or more entries fail.                                                                                                                     |
| `Config.hasPath(fileKey)`              | Registry lookup. Returns `true` when the key is registered, `false` otherwise. Does not fall back to `homeConfig`.                                                                                                       |
| `Config.pathFor(fileKey)`              | Returns the resolved physical path for a key. Unknown keys fall back to the `homeConfig` path.                                                                                                                           |
| `Config.updatePath(fileKey, fsPath)`   | Changes the physical path of an existing non-default key, discards its old document, and loads the new file. Rejects `homeConfig`, unregistered keys, empty paths, active write pipelines, and duplicate physical paths. |
| `Config.removePath(fileKey)`           | Removes a non-default key plus its document, state, and watcher. Leaves the physical file untouched. Rejects `homeConfig`, unregistered keys, and active write pipelines.                                                |

| Example                                                                  | Result                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Config.registerPath("networkConfig", "~/.config/N0ctOS/network.json")`  | `true` and key registered plus controller created; `true` when already registered with the same path; `false` on empty key/path, conflicting path, or duplicate physical path                                                                     |
| `Config.registerPaths({networkConfig: "~/.config/N0ctOS/network.json"})` | `true` when every entry registered; `false` when one or more entries failed or the table is not an object                                                                                                                                         |
| `Config.hasPath("networkConfig")`                                        | `true` when registered, `false` otherwise (no fallback)                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `Config.pathFor("networkConfig")`                                        | Resolved path, e.g. `"/home/user/.config/N0ctOS/network.json"`; `homeConfig` path when the key is unknown                                                                                                                                         |
| `Config.updatePath("networkConfig", "~/.config/N0ctOS/network-v2.json")` | `true` and mapping replaced plus old document discarded plus new file loaded; `false` for `homeConfig`, unregistered keys, active write pipeline (writing/writePending/queued — baseline-dirty alone does not block), or duplicate physical paths |
| `Config.removePath("networkConfig")`                                     | `true` and registry entry, document, state, and watcher removed (physical file remains); `false` for `homeConfig`, unregistered keys, or active write pipeline                                                                                    |

Path expansion understands:

```text
~
$HOME
${HOME}
$XDG_CONFIG_HOME
${XDG_CONFIG_HOME}
```

Relative paths resolve relative to the home directory.

## Signals

| How to listen                          | What does it do                                                       |
| -------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Config.documentChanged(fileKey)`      | Emitted when a document is replaced (local write or external reload). |
| `Config.externalReload()`              | Emitted when any file finishes an external reload.                    |
| `Config.externalReloadFor(fileKey)`    | Emitted when the given file finishes an external reload.              |
| `Config.saveError(reason)`             | Emitted when any file fails to save or create its directory.          |
| `Config.saveErrorFor(fileKey, reason)` | Emitted when the given file fails to save or create its directory.    |

### Typical component usage

```qml
readonly property bool isDnd:
    Config.get(
        "notifications.isDnd",
        false
    )

readonly property int volume:
    Config.get(
        "audio.volume",
        100
    )

readonly property var wifiEnabled:
    Config.get(
        "wifi.enabled",
        true,
        "networkConfig"
    )
```

That is the intended everyday usage.

Components normally should not need to know how documents, file keys, watchers, or the save queue work.

***

# 3. IPC API

IPC target:

```text
n0ctos-config
```

The IPC layer exposes high-level configuration operations. A terminal command does not need to know about `FileView`, JSON parsing, watchers, write queues, atomic writes, or document objects.

## Core CRUD

| How to call                           | What does it do                                                                           |
| ------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `get <dataPath>`                      | Reads a value from `homeConfig` as JSON. Returns `""` when missing.                       |
| `getDocument`                         | Reads the whole `homeConfig` document as JSON. Returns `""` on failure.                   |
| `has <dataPath>`                      | Checks whether a value exists in `homeConfig`.                                            |
| `setJson <dataPath> <json>`           | Parses `<json>` and writes it to `homeConfig`.                                            |
| `updateJson <dataPath> <json-object>` | Deep-merges a JSON object value into a `homeConfig` data path. Rejects non-object values. |
| `remove <dataPath>`                   | Deletes a value from `homeConfig`.                                                        |

| Example                                                               | Result                                                                                              |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `qs ipc call n0ctos-config get notifications.isDnd`                   | `"true"` (JSON value), or `""` when missing                                                         |
| `qs ipc call n0ctos-config has notifications.isDnd`                   | `"true"` when it exists, `"false"` when it does not                                                 |
| `qs ipc call n0ctos-config setJson notifications.isDnd true`          | `"true"` and value written plus autosave write queued; `"false"` on invalid JSON or rejected write  |
| `qs ipc call n0ctos-config updateJson notifications '{"isDnd":true}'` | `"true"` and value merged plus autosave write queued; `"false"` on invalid JSON or non-object value |
| `qs ipc call n0ctos-config remove notifications.isDnd`                | `"true"` and property deleted plus autosave write queued; `"false"` when the path does not exist    |

`<json>` must be valid JSON.

For example:

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-config setJson \
    notifications \
    '{"isDnd":true,"timeout":5}'
```

Boolean:

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-config setJson \
    notifications.isDnd \
    true
```

Number:

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-config setJson \
    audio.volume \
    80
```

String:

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-config setJson \
    wallpaper.mode \
    '"random"'
```

Object value:

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-config updateJson \
    notifications \
    '{"isDnd":true,"timeout":5}'
```

Read a value:

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-config get \
    notifications.isDnd
```

returns:

```text
true
```

or an empty string when the property does not exist.

Check existence:

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-config has \
    notifications.isDnd
```

returns:

```text
true
```

or:

```text
false
```

## State and paths

| How to call   | What does it do                                              |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `isReady`     | Returns whether `homeConfig` is ready.                       |
| `isWriting`   | Returns whether `homeConfig` is writing.                     |
| `isDirty`     | Returns whether `homeConfig` has uncommitted change history. |
| `getPath`     | Returns the resolved `homeConfig` path.                      |
| `getRevision` | Returns the `homeConfig` revision number.                    |

| Example                                 | Result                                                   |
| --------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| `qs ipc call n0ctos-config isReady`     | `"true"` when ready, `"false"` otherwise                 |
| `qs ipc call n0ctos-config isWriting`   | `"true"` while writing, `"false"` otherwise              |
| `qs ipc call n0ctos-config isDirty`     | `"true"` when change history exists, `"false"` otherwise |
| `qs ipc call n0ctos-config getPath`     | `"/home/user/.config/N0ctOS/config.json"`                |
| `qs ipc call n0ctos-config getRevision` | `"3"` (current revision number)                          |

For example:

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-config isReady
```

returns:

```text
true
```

or:

```text
false
```

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-config getPath
```

returns:

```text
/home/user/.config/N0ctOS/config.json
```

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-config getRevision
```

returns:

```text
3
```

## File control

| How to call | What does it do                                                                                                               |
| ----------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `save`      | True checkpoint for `homeConfig` (sync when idle, deferred while writes are in flight; see Undo history).                     |
| `reload`    | Reloads `homeConfig`, discarding unsaved state (baseline = disk, history wiped). Rejected while the write pipeline is active. |
| `reloadAll` | Reloads every registered file. Skips files currently being written.                                                           |

| Example                               | Result                                                                                     |
| ------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `qs ipc call n0ctos-config save`      | `"true"` checkpoint (sync or deferred); `"false"` when no controller exists or not ready   |
| `qs ipc call n0ctos-config reload`    | `"true"` and file reloaded; `"false"` while writing or when no controller exists           |
| `qs ipc call n0ctos-config reloadAll` | `"true"` when every file reloaded; `"false"` when one or more files were skipped or failed |

For example:

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-config save
```

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-config reload
```

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-config reloadAll
```

## Registry

| How to call                     | What does it do                                                                       |
| ------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `hasPath <fileKey>`             | Checks whether a file key is registered. No fallback.                                 |
| `getPaths`                      | Returns all registered paths as a JSON string. Returns `""` on serialization failure. |
| `registerPath <fileKey> <path>` | Registers one logical file key.                                                       |
| `updatePath <fileKey> <path>`   | Redirects an existing non-default key to a new physical path.                         |
| `removePath <fileKey>`          | Removes a non-default key. Leaves the physical file untouched.                        |

| Example                                                                                 | Result                                                                             |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `qs ipc call n0ctos-config hasPath networkConfig`                                       | `"true"` when registered, `"false"` otherwise                                      |
| `qs ipc call n0ctos-config getPaths`                                                    | `'{"homeConfig":"/home/user/.config/N0ctOS/config.json",...}'`, or `""` on failure |
| `qs ipc call n0ctos-config registerPath networkConfig '~/.config/N0ctOS/network.json'`  | `"true"` and key registered; `"false"` when rejected                               |
| `qs ipc call n0ctos-config updatePath networkConfig '~/.config/N0ctOS/network-v2.json'` | `"true"` and path replaced plus new file loaded; `"false"` when rejected           |
| `qs ipc call n0ctos-config removePath networkConfig`                                    | `"true"` and registry entry removed (file remains); `"false"` when rejected        |

For example:

```bash
qs ipc call \
    n0ctos-config \
    hasPath \
    networkConfig
```

returns:

```text
true
```

when the key is registered.

```bash
qs ipc call \
    n0ctos-config \
    getPaths
```

returns:

```json
{
    "homeConfig": "/home/user/.config/N0ctOS/config.json",
    "networkConfig": "/home/user/.config/N0ctOS/network.json"
}
```

```bash
qs ipc call \
    n0ctos-config \
    registerPath \
    networkConfig \
    '~/.config/N0ctOS/network.json'
```

```bash
qs ipc call \
    n0ctos-config \
    updatePath \
    networkConfig \
    '~/.config/N0ctOS/network-v2.json'
```

This changes the physical path associated with `networkConfig`. It does not move or copy the old file.

```bash
qs ipc call \
    n0ctos-config \
    removePath \
    networkConfig
```

This removes the logical registry entry and its watcher. It does not delete the physical file.

## File-specific operations

| How to call                                       | What does it do                                                                                               |
| ------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `isReadyAt <fileKey>`                             | Returns whether the given file is ready. Unknown keys fall back to `homeConfig`.                              |
| `isWritingAt <fileKey>`                           | Returns whether the given file is writing. Unknown keys fall back to `homeConfig`.                            |
| `isDirtyAt <fileKey>`                             | Returns whether the given file is dirty. Unknown keys fall back to `homeConfig`.                              |
| `getPathAt <fileKey>`                             | Returns the resolved path for the given key. Unknown keys fall back to the `homeConfig` path.                 |
| `getRevisionAt <fileKey>`                         | Returns the revision for the given key. Unknown keys fall back to `homeConfig`.                               |
| `getAt <path> <fileKey>`                          | Reads a value from the given file as JSON. Returns `""` when missing. Unknown keys fall back to `homeConfig`. |
| `hasAt <path> <fileKey>`                          | Checks existence in the given file. Unknown keys fall back to `homeConfig`.                                   |
| `setJsonAt <path> <json> <fileKey>`               | Writes parsed JSON to the given file. Unknown keys fall back to `homeConfig`.                                 |
| `updateJsonAt <dataPath> <json-object> <fileKey>` | Merges an object value into the given file. Unknown keys fall back to `homeConfig`.                           |
| `removeAt <path> <fileKey>`                       | Deletes a value from the given file. Unknown keys fall back to `homeConfig`.                                  |
| `saveAt <fileKey>`                                | Saves the given file.                                                                                         |
