```qml
)
```

prefers `default`, then falls back to the first available action.

### Inline replies

Notifications supporting inline replies can be replied to through the service.

Check:

```qml
notification.hasInlineReply
```

and read the suggested placeholder:

```qml
notification.inlineReplyPlaceholder
```

Reply:

```qml
Notifications.reply(
    notification.id,
    replyInput.text
)
```

### Images and icons

The service preserves notification image and icon information required by the UI and persistent history.

Important fields include:

```text
appIcon
image
desktopEntry
```

Live UI uses native properties. Persistent history uses stored snapshot values.

### Replacement notifications

When an application updates a notification using its existing notification ID, the service keeps the same logical notification instead of treating it as an entirely new notification.

This is especially useful for:

```text
download progress
media state
battery status
message updates
progress notifications
```

The history entry is updated in place. No second popup is created. No second unseen increment occurs.

### Config integration

Notification configuration lives under:

```json
{
    "notifications": {
        "historySize": 100,
        "dnd": false,
        "popupTimeout": {
            "low": 3,
            "normal": 5
        },
        "grouping": {
            "enabled": true
        }
    }
}
```

Game Mode is separate:

```json
{
    "isGameMode": false
}
```

That separation is intentional.

### No polling for notification state

Notification changes are handled through native signals and observers.

The popup timer only checks timed popup descriptors every `100ms` while timed popups exist.

It is not a polling loop over applications.

***

## Limitations

### Only standard notification urgencies

Quickshell's native notification urgency model provides:

```text
Low
Normal
Critical
```

N0ctOS does not invent another native urgency level.

Use:

```qml
Notifications.isLow(notification)
Notifications.isNormal(notification)
Notifications.isCritical(notification)
```

or:

```qml
Notifications.urgencyName(
    notification
)
```

### Popup lifetime is separate from notification lifetime

A popup timing out does not dismiss the underlying notification.

```text
popup → gone
notification → alive
```

To actually close a notification, use:

```qml
Notifications.dismiss(
    notificationId
)
```

or:

```qml
Notifications.expire(
    notificationId
)
```

### No notification sounds

Notification sound handling is not part of this service.

A future `Sfx.qml` service can own notification sound behavior.

### Game Mode is external

Notifications reads (via `Notifications.isGameMode`):

```qml
Config.get("isGameMode")
```

but does not own that state.

Do not try to change Game Mode through Notifications.

### No per-notification read state

There is one service-level unseen counter rather than an `isRead` value on every notification.

```text
_unseenCount += 1
        ↓
markAllRead()
        ↓
_unseenCount = 0
```

### History stores snapshots

History does not retain live `Notification` objects indefinitely.

This is intentional so persistent data remains simple and safe to serialize.

```text
active
    live notification object

history
    plain persistent snapshot
```

### IPC cannot return live objects

The terminal caller does not receive the live `Notification` object itself.

The actual live object is only available to QML code through:

```qml
Notifications.active
Notifications.popups
```

IPC returns serializable snapshots through `activeData()`, `historyData()`, and `popupData()`.

### Critical timeout is immutable

`setPopupTimeout` accepts only:

```text
low
normal
```

`critical` always returns:

```text
0
```

Unknown urgency names return:

```text
-1
```

***

# 5. Example use cases

## 5.1 Basic notification list

A normal notification list can be implemented entirely from `Notifications.active`.

```qml
import QtQuick
import Quickshell

import qs.services

ListView {
    anchors.fill: parent

    spacing: 8

    model:
        Notifications.active

    delegate: Rectangle {
        required property var modelData

        width:
            ListView.view.width

        height:
            92

        radius:
            12

        color:
            "#101720"

        border.width:
            1

        border.color:
            "#263541"

        Column {
            anchors.fill:
                parent

            anchors.margins:
                12

            spacing:
                4

            Text {
                text:
                    modelData.appName ||
                    "Application"

                color:
                    "#91a1b2"

                font.pixelSize:
                    10
            }

            Text {
                text:
                    modelData.summary ||
                    "Notification"

                color:
                    "#ffffff"

                font.pixelSize:
                    14

                font.bold:
                    true
            }

            Text {
                width:
                    parent.width

                text:
                    modelData.body ||
                    ""

                color:
                    "#91a1b2"

                font.pixelSize:
                    11

                wrapMode:
                    Text.WordWrap

                maximumLineCount:
                    3
            }
        }
    }
}
```

`modelData` is the live Quickshell `Notification` object.

***

## 5.2 Notification badge in a top bar

A top bar can show an indicator whenever something unseen exists.

```qml
import QtQuick
import Quickshell

import qs.services

Item {
    width: 32
    height: 32

    Text {
        anchors.centerIn:
            parent

        text:
            "󰂚"

        color:
            Notifications.hasUnseen
                ? "#2acfff"
                : "#91a1b2"

        font.family:
            "Symbols Nerd Font"

        font.pixelSize:
            19
    }

    Rectangle {
        visible:
            Notifications.hasUnseen

        width:
            Notifications.unseenCount > 9
                ? 20
                : 8

        height:
            18

        radius:
            9

        anchors {
            right: parent.right
            top: parent.top
        }

        color:
            "#2acfff"

        Text {
            visible:
                Notifications.unseenCount > 9

            anchors.centerIn:
                parent

            text:
                Notifications.unseenCount > 99
                    ? "99+"
                    : String(
                        Notifications.unseenCount
                    )

            color:
                "#061018"

            font.pixelSize:
                8

            font.bold:
                true
        }
    }
}
```

***

## 5.3 Opening the notification hub

The usual interaction is:

```text
user clicks notification icon
        ↓
hub opens
        ↓
markAllRead()
```

Example:

```qml
MouseArea {
    anchors.fill:
        parent

    onClicked: {
        notificationHub.visible = true

        Notifications.markAllRead()
    }
}
```

This does not clear the notifications.

It only clears the unseen counter.

***

## 5.4 DND button

```qml
Rectangle {
    width: 180
    height: 44

    radius: 10

    color:
        Notifications.isDnd
            ? "#302516"
            : "#15222b"

    Text {
        anchors.centerIn:
            parent

        text:
            Notifications.isDnd
                ? "󰂛  Do Not Disturb"
                : "󰂚  Notifications"

        color:
            Notifications.isDnd
                ? "#ffb454"
                : "#ffffff"

        font.family:
            "Symbols Nerd Font"

        font.pixelSize:
            12
    }

    MouseArea {
        anchors.fill:
            parent

        onClicked:
            Notifications.toggleDnd()
    }
}
```

For explicit control:

```qml
Notifications.setDnd(
    !Notifications.isDnd
)
```

***

## 5.5 Popup UI

A popup UI should use:

```qml
Notifications.popups
```

rather than trying to determine popup eligibility itself.

```qml
ListView {
    width: 420

    spacing: 10

    model:
        Notifications.popups

    delegate: Rectangle {
        required property var modelData

        width:
            ListView.view.width

        implicitHeight:
            contentColumn.implicitHeight +
            28

        radius:
            14

        color:
            "#101720"

        border.width:
            1

        border.color:
            "#263541"

        Column {
            id: contentColumn

            anchors {
                top: parent.top
                left: parent.left
                right: parent.right
            }

            anchors.margins:
                14

            spacing:
                7

            Text {
                text:
                    modelData.notification.appName ||
                    "Application"

                color:
                    "#91a1b2"

                font.pixelSize:
                    10
            }

            Text {
                text:
                    modelData.notification.summary ||
                    "Notification"

                color:
                    "#ffffff"

                font.pixelSize:
                    14

                font.bold:
                    true
            }

            Text {
                width:
                    parent.width

                text:
                    modelData.notification.body ||
                    ""

                color:
                    "#91a1b2"

                font.pixelSize:
                    11

                wrapMode:
                    Text.WordWrap
            }
        }
    }
}
```

The popup component does not decide:

```text
whether DND is active
whether Game Mode is active
whether the urgency is allowed
how long the popup should live
```

The service has already made those decisions.

***

## 5.6 Actions and inline replies

A notification may contain actions.

```qml
Row {
    spacing: 6

    Repeater {
        model:
            notification.actions

        delegate: Rectangle {
            required property var modelData

            width: 100
            height: 34

            radius: 8
            color: "#17212b"

            Text {
                anchors.centerIn: parent

                text:
                    modelData.text

                color: "white"
            }

            MouseArea {
                anchors.fill: parent

                onClicked:
                    modelData.invoke()
            }
        }
    }
}
```

Or use identifiers:

```qml
Notifications.invokeAction(
    notification.id,
    "default"
)
```

For the common open behavior:

```qml
Notifications.invokeDefaultAction(
    notification.id
)
```

For inline replies:

```qml
Row {
    visible:
        notification.hasInlineReply

    spacing: 6

    TextField {
        id: replyInput

        width: 260

        placeholderText:
            notification.inlineReplyPlaceholder ||
            "Reply..."
    }

    Button {
        text: "Send"

        onClicked: {
            Notifications.reply(
                notification.id,
                replyInput.text
            )

            replyInput.clear()
        }
    }
}
```

***

## 5.7 Grouped history hub

A hub can combine history, grouping, and DND controls.

```qml
ListView {
    anchors.fill: parent

    model:
        Notifications.groupedByApps

    delegate: Column {
        required property var modelData

        Text {
            text:
                modelData.label +
                " (" +
                modelData.count +
                ")"
        }

        Repeater {
            model:
                modelData.items

            delegate: Text {
                required property var modelData

                text:
                    modelData.summary
            }
        }
    }
}
```

The available groupings are:

```qml
Notifications.groupedByApps
Notifications.groupedByDate
Notifications.groupedByUrgency
```

The terminal equivalents are:

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-notifications groups apps
```

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-notifications groups dates
```

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-notifications groups urgency
```

***

## 5.8 Testing DND behavior

Send a normal notification:

```bash
notify-send -u normal "Normal" "This should popup when DND is off."
```

Enable DND:

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-notifications setDnd true
```

Send another normal notification:

```bash
notify-send -u normal "Normal" "This should not popup."
```

Send a critical notification:

```bash
notify-send -u critical "Critical" "This should still popup."
```

The expected result is:

```text
normal #1
    active ✓
    history ✓
    popup ✓

normal #2
    active ✓
    history ✓
    popup ✗

critical
    active ✓
    history ✓
    popup ✓
```

Test critical persistence:

```bash
notify-send \
    -u critical \
    "Critical Test" \
    "This popup should stay until manually closed."
```

Then inspect:

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-notifications getStatus
```

The popup entry should have:

```text
timeout = 0
```

***

## 5.9 Terminal workflow

Read the service state:

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-notifications getStatus
```

Read active snapshots:

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-notifications active
```

Read history:

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-notifications history
```

Read popups:

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-notifications popups
```

Enable DND:

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-notifications setDnd true
```

Dismiss notification `42`:

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-notifications dismiss 42
```

Remove only its popup:

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-notifications removePopup 42
```

Mark everything read:

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-notifications markAllRead
```

Inspect the complete service again:

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-notifications getStatus
```

***

# 6. Detailed architecture

This section is for developers working on `Notifications.qml` and the services/components that consume it.

***

## 6.1 Overall architecture

The service is the single notification owner for N0ctOS.

```text
Applications
    │
    │ org.freedesktop.Notifications
    ▼
NotificationServer
    │
    ▼
Notifications.qml
    │
    ├── Active notifications
    ├── Persistent history
    ├── Popup policy
    ├── Popup lifetime
    ├── Unseen state
    ├── Actions
    ├── Inline replies
    ├── Grouping
    ├── DND
    └── IPC
    │
    ▼
N0ctOS UI
```

There are effectively two responsibilities:

```text
Notifications
    notification logic and presentation policy

Config + FileView
    configuration persistence and history persistence
```

Notifications should not duplicate functionality already provided by those persistence systems.

***

## 6.2 Native notification server

The service contains one:

```qml
NotificationServer {
    id: notificationServer
}
```

The server advertises the notification capabilities required by N0ctOS:

```qml
actionsSupported: true
bodySupported: true
bodyHyperlinksSupported: true
bodyMarkupSupported: true
bodyImagesSupported: true
imageSupported: true
actionIconsSupported: true
inlineReplySupported: true
persistenceSupported: true
keepOnReload: true
```

The notification server receives notifications through:

```qml
onNotification: function(notification) {
    root._receiveNotification(
        notification
    )
}
```

***

## 6.3 The `tracked = true` requirement

One of the most important details in the whole service is:

```qml
notification.tracked = true
```

This must happen when a notification is received.

Conceptually:

```text
notification arrives
        │
        ▼
onNotification
        │
        ▼
tracked = true
        │
        ▼
notification remains alive
```

Without tracking it, the notification can be discarded by the native notification server after the callback returns.

Therefore `_receiveNotification()` must make tracking the first important operation.

***

## 6.4 Active is native state

The service does not maintain a second JavaScript copy of active notifications.

Instead:

```qml
Notifications.active
```

maps directly to:

```qml
notificationServer.trackedNotifications
```

This matters because `trackedNotifications` contains the live native `Notification` objects.

The UI therefore receives real objects rather than stale copies.

The conceptual model is:

```text
NotificationServer
        │
        ▼
trackedNotifications
        │
        ├── Notification A
        ├── Notification B
        └── Notification C
```

For JavaScript processing:

```qml
Notifications.activeList
```

exposes:

```text
trackedNotifications.values
```

For counts only:

```qml
Notifications.activeCount
```

exposes:

```text
trackedNotifications.values.length
```

***

## 6.5 History is separate from active

Active notifications cannot simply be written directly to disk because native notification objects are not the persistent representation we want.

History therefore uses snapshots:

```text
live Notification
       │
       ▼
snapshot object
       │
       ▼
JSON
```

This gives the service two clear representations:

```text
active
    live

history
    persistent snapshot
```

***

## 6.6 History storage

The persistent file uses:

```qml
Quickshell.dataPath(
    "notifications.json"
)
```

The file is owned by the service.

The UI never writes to it.

The stored structure is conceptually:

```json
{
    "version": 1,
    "unseenCount": 3,
    "items": [
        {
            "notificationId": 12,
            "appName": "Discord",
            "summary": "New message",
            "body": "Hello"
        }
    ]
}
```

The service can change its internal representation in the future by increasing the version.

The file uses:

```qml
blockLoading: true
watchChanges: false
```

so history can be synchronously consumed once the `FileView` is ready.

***

## 6.7 History entries are lifecycle records

A history entry does not disappear merely because a popup expires.

For example:

```text
notification arrives
        │
        ├── history created
        ├── active created
        └── popup created
```

Then:

```text
popup expires
        │
        └── popup removed

history → still present
active  → still present
```

Only when the actual notification closes does history become marked as closed.

This gives the hub enough information to distinguish:

```text
currently active
previously closed
```

A history entry contains information such as:

```json
{
    "notificationId": 42,
    "receivedAt": 1760000000000,
    "closedAt": null,
    "isClosed": false,
    "closeReason": "",
    "closeReasonCode": 0,
    "appName": "Discord",
    "summary": "New message",
    "body": "Someone sent you a message.",
    "urgency": 1,
    "resident": false,
    "transient": false,
    "hasInlineReply": false,
    "actions": []
}
```

***

## 6.8 Snapshot update strategy

When a notification is received:

```text
find history entry by notification ID
```

If it does not exist:

```text
create one
```

If it already exists:

```text
update the existing entry
```

That second case is important for replacement notifications.

The notification ID is therefore the stable identity used by the service.

New entries are inserted newest-first:

```text
_history.unshift(snapshot)
```

and trimmed to:

```text
_history.slice(0, historySize)
```

***

## 6.9 Replacement notifications

Applications are allowed to send another notification using an existing notification ID.

Conceptually:

```text
first notification
    ID = 42
       │
       ▼
history entry #42
active object #42
popup #42
```

Application sends replacement:

```text
second notification
    ID = 42
       │
       ▼
same native Notification
updated
```

The service should not intentionally create:

```text
notification #43
```

just because the content changed.

Instead:

```text
ID 42
 │
 ├── summary changes
 ├── body changes
 ├── actions change
 └── image changes
```

The UI delegate can therefore remain associated with the same notification object.

***

## 6.10 Notification observers

The service creates lightweight `Connections` objects for the live notification objects.

Their job is to notice changes such as:

```text
summary
body
appName
appIcon
urgency
actions
image
inline reply state
close signal
```

The general flow is:

```text
Notification object changes
        │
        ▼
observer signal
        │
        ▼
service updates snapshot
        │
        ▼
history remains synchronized
```

This avoids polling.

The service does not repeatedly ask every notification whether something changed.

***

## 6.11 Observer lifetime

Observers exist only while the notification is alive.

The lifecycle is:

```text
notification created
        │
        ▼
observer created
        │
        ▼
notification changes
        │
        ▼
observer reacts
        │
        ▼
notification closes
        │
        ▼
observer released
```

This is important because retaining observer objects forever would create unnecessary resource usage.

***

## 6.12 Close signal

Native notifications provide a `closed(reason)` signal.

When it fires, the service:

```text
1. identifies the notification
2. records the close reason
3. records the close time
4. marks its history entry closed
5. removes its popup
6. saves history
7. releases the observer
```

The service keeps both:

```text
closeReason
closeReasonCode
```

so the UI can use readable text while the underlying numeric value remains available.

***

## 6.13 Close reasons

The native notification system provides reasons such as:

```text
Expired
Dismissed
CloseRequested
```

The service converts these into readable strings:

```text
expired
dismissed
close-requested
```

Unknown values are represented safely as:

```text
unknown
```

***

## 6.14 Popup state is presentation state

The service deliberately keeps popup state separate from active state.

This is one of the central architectural rules.

```text
active
    = actual notification

popup
    = current presentation of notification
```

A popup descriptor therefore contains a reference to the live notification:

```qml
{
    notification: notification,
    notificationId: notification.id,

    timeout: 5,

    startedAt: ...,
    expiresAt: ...
}
```

The descriptor is not itself the notification.

***

## 6.15 Popup creation

After receiving the notification, the service performs:

```text
receive
   │
   ├── track
   ├── observe
   ├── history
   ├── unseen
   │
   ▼
popup policy
```

If the policy says the notification should popup:

```text
_addPopup(notification)
```

creates the descriptor.

If not:

```text
no popup descriptor is created
```

The notification is still retained in active/history.

Newest popups appear first:

```text
_popups.unshift(entry)
```

A replacement ID never creates a second popup for the same notification.

***

## 6.16 Exact popup policy

The policy is intentionally simple:

```qml
function _shouldPopup(notification) {
    if (root.isGameMode)
        return false

    if (root.isDnd)
        return root.isCritical(
            notification
        )

    return true
}
```

That means there is no complicated priority system hidden inside the popup decision.

The result is exactly:

```text
Game Mode
    → no popups

Game Mode off + DND on
    → critical only

Game Mode off + DND off
    → all
```

***

## 6.17 Why Game Mode is checked first

Game Mode is an absolute popup suppression state.

Therefore:

```text
Game Mode = true
DND = false
critical = true
```

still results in:

```text
no popup
```

Game Mode wins because it is intended to completely suppress popup presentation.

***

## 6.18 Why DND does not suppress storage

DND is a presentation policy.

It should not change the notification intake pipeline.

Therefore when DND is enabled:

```text
notification arrives
        │
        ├── active ✓
        ├── history ✓
        ├── unseen ✓
        └── popup?
                │
                ├── critical → yes
                └── other    → no
```

This means the user can later open the notification hub and see what arrived while DND was active.

***

## 6.19 Popup timeouts

Low and normal popup timeout values are configurable.

The defaults are:

```text
low      = 3 seconds
normal   = 5 seconds
critical = 0
```

Critical uses zero because:

```text
0
```

means:

```text
no automatic popup expiration
```

The service never uses the critical timeout as a countdown.

`low` and `normal` have a minimum of:

```text
0.1 seconds
```

***

## 6.20 Popup expiration is not notification expiration

This is an important distinction.

When a normal popup expires:

```text
popupExpiryTimer
        │
        ▼
remove popup descriptor
```

The service does **not** call:

```qml
notification.expire()
```

Therefore:

```text
popup → gone
notification → alive
```

This allows active notifications to remain in the notification hub after their popup disappears.

***

## 6.21 Popup timer implementation

The service uses one lightweight timer to check timed popup descriptors.

```qml
Timer {
    interval: 100
    repeat: true

    running:
        root._hasTimedPopups()

    onTriggered:
        root._expirePopups()
}
```

The timer is only active if a popup has:

```text
timeout > 0
```

A critical popup has:

```text
timeout = 0
```

so it does not need automatic timeout checking.

This timer is only for popup presentation.

It is not a polling loop over applications or the notification system.

***

## 6.22 Dynamic popup policy changes

The popup list must also respond when policy changes.

For example:

```text
popup visible
       │
       ▼
Game Mode enabled
       │
       ▼
popup policy becomes "none"
       │
       ▼
popup removed
```

Similarly, when DND becomes enabled:

```text
normal popup
       │
       ▼
DND ON
       │
       ▼
normal no longer allowed
       │
       ▼
popup removed
```

The underlying notification remains active.

This is why `_applyPopupPolicy()` operates on popup descriptors rather than modifying active notifications.

***

## 6.23 Unseen state

The service keeps:

```qml
property int _unseenCount
```

rather than attaching an `isRead` property to each notification.

When a new notification arrives:

```text
_unseenCount += 1
```

When the hub marks everything read:

```text
_unseenCount = 0
```

This keeps the read-state model extremely simple.

`lastGeneration` restorations do not increment unseen.

***

## 6.24 Reload handling

The server uses:

```qml
keepOnReload: true
```

so notifications can survive Quickshell reloads.

Restored notifications can be identified using:

```qml
notification.lastGeneration
```

The service does not treat them like fresh events.

For a restored notification:

```text
active
    restored

history
    retained/updated

unseen
    not incremented

popup
    not recreated as a new popup
```

This avoids notification spam whenever the shell reloads.

***

## 6.25 Action routing

The service provides a high-level action API:

```qml
Notifications.invokeAction(
    id,
    identifier
)
```

Internally it:

```text
1. finds the active notification
2. searches its actions
3. finds the requested identifier
4. invokes the action
```

The UI does not need to know how the active notification is located.

Empty identifiers and missing actions return:

```text
false
```

***

## 6.26 Default action routing

`invokeDefaultAction()` first searches for:

```text
default
```

If present:

```text
invoke it
```

Otherwise the service may use the first available action.

This makes simple popup cards easy to implement because they can simply offer:

```text
Open
```

without duplicating action lookup logic.

***

## 6.27 Inline reply routing

The inline reply API follows the same principle.

UI code calls:

```qml
Notifications.reply(
    id,
    text
)
```

The service:

```text
finds live notification
        ↓
checks inline reply support
        ↓
sends reply
```

The service owns this routing; the UI owns only the text field and presentation.

Replies to notifications without `hasInlineReply` return:

```text
false
```

***

## 6.28 Images and icons

Notification snapshots preserve the information needed to reproduce the notification later.

Important fields include:

```text
appIcon
image
desktopEntry
```

Live notification UI can use the corresponding native properties.

Persistent history uses the stored snapshot values.

The service does not create a separate image cache or media subsystem.

That keeps notification storage focused on notification data.

***

## 6.29 Grouping implementation

Grouping is derived from one source:

```text
_history
```

The service does not maintain three independent data stores.

Instead:

```text
_history
   │
   ├── groupedByApps
   ├── groupedByDate
   └── groupedByUrgency
```

Each grouping operation builds temporary buckets.

For example:

```qml
{
    key: "Discord",
    label: "Discord",
    count: 4,
    items: [
        ...
    ]
}
```

When grouping is disabled:

```text
groupedByApps = []
groupedByDate = []
groupedByUrgency = []
```

This keeps history as the single source of truth.

***

## 6.30 Configuration

Notification configuration lives under:

```json
{
    "notifications": {
        "historySize": 100,

        "dnd": false,

        "popupTimeout": {
            "low": 3,
            "normal": 5
        },

        "grouping": {
            "enabled": true
        }
    }
}
```

Game Mode is separate:

```json
{
    "isGameMode": false
}
```

That separation is intentional.

`historySize` is clamped to:

```text
1 … 5000
```

Popup timeouts are clamped to a minimum of:

```text
0.1
```

***

## 6.31 Configuration ownership

The service owns notification settings such as:

```text
historySize
dnd
popupTimeout
grouping
```

Another service owns:

```text
isGameMode
```

Therefore Notifications should not write:

```text
isGameMode
```

when changing its own state.

It only reads it.

Writes flow through:

```qml
Config.set(
    "notifications",
    merged
)
```

***

## 6.32 Reactive state

The service consumes the reactive `Config` document.

Conceptually:

```text
config file changes
        │
        ▼
Config document changes
        │
        ▼
Notifications state reevaluates
        │
        ▼
component bindings reevaluate
```

A component does not need to manually reload notification configuration.

For example:

```qml
readonly property bool silenced:
    Notifications.isDnd
```

can react to configuration changes through the service.

Changing `historySize` trims history immediately and persists the result.

***

## 6.33 IPC architecture

IPC sits above the service API.

The flow is:

```text
terminal / shell module
        │
        ▼
n0ctos-notifications
        │
        ▼
Notifications.qml
```

The IPC functions translate simple external arguments into service operations.

Example:

```text
IPC:

dismiss 42

        ↓

Notifications.dismiss(42)
```

This keeps the external interface simple while allowing the internal service to evolve.

Serialization follows:

```text
QML objects → snapshots → JSON strings
```

for `active`, `history`, `popups`, and `groups`.

***

## 6.34 Why IPC should stay high-level

IPC callers should not have to understand:

```text
NotificationServer
trackedNotifications
observer objects
history JSON
popup descriptors
timer state
```

Those are implementation details.

A caller should only need:

```text
dismiss
expire
reply
toggleDnd
getStatus
```

This preserves a clean service boundary.

***

## 6.35 Complete notification lifecycle

The full lifecycle is:

```text
Application
    │
    │ notify-send / D-Bus
    ▼
NotificationServer
    │
    │ onNotification
    ▼
_receiveNotification()
    │
    ├── tracked = true
    │
    ├── observer created
    │
    ├── history inserted/updated
    │
    ├── unseen incremented
    │
    ▼
_shouldPopup()
    │
    ├── Game Mode
    │      └── no popup
    │
    ├── DND
    │      └── critical only
    │
    └── normal
           └── all
    │
    ▼
_addPopup()
    │
    ├── timed popup
    │
    └── critical popup
    │
    ▼
UI consumes Notifications.popups
    │
    ├── timer expires
    │      └── popup removed
    │
    └── user closes
           └── dismiss / expire
    │
    ▼
actual notification close
    │
    ▼
closed(reason)
    │
    ├── history finalized
    ├── popup removed
    ├── history persisted
    └── observer destroyed
```

***

## 6.36 The three-model design

The most important mental model for developers is:

```text
                    Notification
                         │
             ┌───────────┼───────────┐
             │           │           │
             ▼           ▼           ▼
          active      history      popup
           live       snapshot    descriptor
```

### `active`

Answers:

> What notifications are alive right now?

### `history`

Answers:

> What notifications has the shell recorded?

### `popups`

Answers:

> What notifications should currently be presented as popup UI?

None of these should be collapsed into one model.

***

## 6.37 What UI / service code should not do

UI components should not:

```text
create NotificationServer

track notifications independently

implement their own DND logic

check Game Mode themselves to decide popup eligibility

write notifications.json

implement replacement-ID handling

implement notification persistence

poll notification state

manually maintain popup timeout state

call the native notification API when a Notifications API exists
```

Instead, UI code should use the service.

For example:

```qml
// Good

model:
    Notifications.popups
```

rather than:

```qml
// Bad

NotificationServer {
    ...
}
```

Likewise:

```qml
// Good

Notifications.dismiss(
    notification.id
)
```

rather than building another notification-closing abstraction in every UI component.

***

## 6.38 Final architecture summary

At the highest level:

```text
                 ┌──────────────────────┐
                 │      Applications    │
                 └──────────┬───────────┘
                            │
                            │ D-Bus
                            ▼
                 ┌──────────────────────┐
                 │  NotificationServer  │
                 └──────────┬───────────┘
                            │
                            ▼
                 ┌──────────────────────┐
                 │ Notifications.qml    │
                 │                      │
                 │  active              │
                 │  history             │
                 │  popups              │
                 │  unseen              │
                 │  DND                 │
                 │  actions             │
                 │  replies             │
                 │  grouping            │
                 │  IPC                 │
                 └──────────┬───────────┘
                            │
             ┌──────────────┼──────────────┐
             │              │              │
             ▼              ▼              ▼
          Top Bar       Popup UI       Notification Hub
```

The core rule is:

> **Receive notifications once, keep their state centralized, decide when they should be presented, and expose a clean reactive API to the rest of N0ctOS.**


# Power Service



`Power.qml` is N0ctOS's centralized power and session-action service.

It gives every shell component one consistent place to trigger shutdown, reboot, suspend, hibernate, lock, and logout without invoking `systemctl` / `loginctl` directly.

The service supports system power actions, session lock and logout, session identity (`sessionId`, `user`), detached command execution, a logout guard for missing sessions, and a full IPC interface.

The normal usage pattern is:

```text
Component
    │
    ▼
Power
    │
    ├── session info
    ├── power actions
    └── session actions
    │
    ▼
systemctl / loginctl
    │
    ▼
system / session
```

***

# 1. What does it do?

`Power.qml` maps simple function calls to system commands.

A component can read session identity:

```qml
Power.sessionId
```

```qml
Power.user
```

or trigger an action:

```qml
Power.shutdown()
```

```qml
Power.lock()
```

The mapping is fixed:

```text
Power.shutdown()  -> systemctl poweroff
Power.reboot()    -> systemctl reboot
Power.suspend()   -> systemctl suspend
Power.hibernate() -> systemctl hibernate
Power.lock()      -> loginctl lock-session
Power.logout()    -> loginctl terminate-session <sessionId>
```

So a component can simply do:

```qml
Power.suspend()
```

and not care which command runs underneath.

All actions launch detached and return `true` when the command was launched. `logout()` is the only exception: it returns `false` with a warning when `XDG_SESSION_ID` is unavailable, because there is no session to terminate.

***

# 2. UI API

Import normally:

```qml
import QtQuick
import Quickshell

import qs.services
```

## Core API

| How to call         | What does it do                                                                                                                          |
| ------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Power.sessionId`   | Current session id from `XDG_SESSION_ID`, `""` when missing.                                                                             |
| `Power.user`        | Current user from `USER`, `""` when missing.                                                                                             |
| `Power.shutdown()`  | Runs `systemctl poweroff`. Returns `true` when launched.                                                                                 |
| `Power.reboot()`    | Runs `systemctl reboot`. Returns `true` when launched.                                                                                   |
| `Power.suspend()`   | Runs `systemctl suspend`. Returns `true` when launched.                                                                                  |
| `Power.hibernate()` | Runs `systemctl hibernate`. Returns `true` when launched.                                                                                |
| `Power.lock()`      | Runs `loginctl lock-session`. Returns `true` when launched.                                                                              |
| `Power.logout()`    | Runs `loginctl terminate-session <sessionId>`. Returns `false` with a warning when `sessionId` is empty, otherwise `true` when launched. |

`_run(command)` exists as an internal helper. Components should call the named actions above, not `_run()` directly.

### Typical component usage

```qml
Row {
    spacing: 8

    Button {
        text: "Lock"

        onClicked:
            Power.lock()
    }

    Button {
        text: "Suspend"

        onClicked:
            Power.suspend()
    }

    Button {
        text: "Shutdown"

        onClicked:
            Power.shutdown()
    }
}
```

That is the intended everyday usage.

Components normally should not need to know how `systemctl`, `loginctl`, session ids, or detached execution work.

***

# 3. IPC API

IPC target:

```text
n0ctos-power
```

## Core actions

| How to call | What does it do                                                                                             |
| ----------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `shutdown`  | Runs `systemctl poweroff`. Returns `true` when launched.                                                    |
| `reboot`    | Runs `systemctl reboot`. Returns `true` when launched.                                                      |
| `suspend`   | Runs `systemctl suspend`. Returns `true` when launched.                                                     |
| `hibernate` | Runs `systemctl hibernate`. Returns `true` when launched.                                                   |
| `lock`      | Runs `loginctl lock-session`. Returns `true` when launched.                                                 |
| `logout`    | Runs `loginctl terminate-session <sessionId>`. Returns `false` when `sessionId` is empty, otherwise `true`. |

| Example                              | Result                                                                                                         |
| ------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `qs ipc call n0ctos-power shutdown`  | `true`, system powers off                                                                                      |
| `qs ipc call n0ctos-power reboot`    | `true`, system reboots                                                                                         |
| `qs ipc call n0ctos-power suspend`   | `true`, system suspends                                                                                        |
| `qs ipc call n0ctos-power hibernate` | `true`, system hibernates                                                                                      |
| `qs ipc call n0ctos-power lock`      | `true`, session locks                                                                                          |
| `qs ipc call n0ctos-power logout`    | `true` when `XDG_SESSION_ID` is set, `false` with `[Power] XDG_SESSION_ID is unavailable` warning when missing |

For example:

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-power lock
```

returns:

```text
true
```

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-power shutdown
```

returns:

```text
true
```

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-power logout
```

returns:

```text
true
```

when a session id exists, or:

```text
false
```

with a shell warning when `XDG_SESSION_ID` is unavailable.

***

# 4. Features / limitations

## Features

### Single entry point for power actions

All power and session actions go through:

```text
Power.qml
```

instead of each panel, menu, or keybinding invoking:

```text
systemctl
loginctl
```

directly.

### Detached execution

Every action uses:

```qml
Quickshell.execDetached({
    command: command
})
```

The shell does not block waiting for the power command to finish.

### Session identity

The service exposes:

```text
sessionId <- XDG_SESSION_ID
user      <- USER
```

Both fall back to `""` when the environment variable is missing, so bindings never see `undefined`.

### Logout guard

`logout()` checks:

```text
sessionId empty -> warn + return false
sessionId set   -> terminate-session <sessionId>
```

This avoids running `loginctl terminate-session` with an empty argument.

***

## Limitations

### No confirmation or inhibition handling

The service does not ask for confirmation, check inhibitors, or delay the action.

Calling:

```qml
Power.shutdown()
```

immediately launches:

```text
systemctl poweroff
```

Any confirmation UI must live in the calling component.

### Logout requires `XDG_SESSION_ID`

If the session id is missing:

```qml
Power.logout()
```

returns:

```text
false
```

and logs:

```text
[Power] XDG_SESSION_ID is unavailable
```

It cannot guess which session to terminate.

### `lock()` does not pass a session id

`lock()` runs:

```text
loginctl lock-session
```

with no arguments. It locks the current session as resolved by `loginctl` itself. It does not target `sessionId` explicitly.

### No status or capability queries

The service reports only whether the command was launched (`true` / `false`).

There is no:

```text
canSuspend
canHibernate
isLocked
```

Components cannot ask Power whether suspend or hibernate is supported by the system.

***

# 5. Example use cases

## 5.1 A power menu

Each button maps directly to one service call:

```qml
import QtQuick
import Quickshell

import qs.services

Column {
    spacing: 8

    Button {
        text: "Shutdown"

        onClicked:
            Power.shutdown()
    }

    Button {
        text: "Reboot"

        onClicked:
            Power.reboot()
    }

    Button {
        text: "Suspend"

        onClicked:
            Power.suspend()
    }

    Button {
        text: "Hibernate"

        onClicked:
            Power.hibernate()
    }
}
```

Each call returns `true` when the detached command was launched.

***

## 5.2 Session lock and logout

Lock needs no session id, logout does:

```qml
import QtQuick

import qs.services

Row {
    spacing: 8

    Button {
        text: "Lock"

        onClicked:
            Power.lock()
    }

    Button {
        text: "Logout"

        enabled:
            Power.sessionId !== ""

        onClicked:
            Power.logout()
    }

    Text {
        visible:
            Power.sessionId === ""

        text:
            "Logout unavailable: no session"
    }
}
```

The result is:

```text
sessionId set   -> logout enabled, returns true
sessionId empty -> logout disabled, would return false
```

***

## 5.3 Terminal workflow

Lock the session:

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-power lock
```

Suspend:

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-power suspend
```

Reboot:

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-power reboot
```

Shut down:

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-power shutdown
```

Log out the current session:

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-power logout
```

***

# 6. Detailed architecture

This section is for developers working on `Power.qml` and the services/components that consume it.

***

## 6.1 Overall architecture

The service is a thin action layer over `systemctl` and `loginctl`:

```text
N0ctOS Component / Service
            │
            ▼
        Power.qml
            │
     ┌──────┼────────┐
     │      │        │
     ▼      ▼        ▼
 session  power   session
 info    actions  actions
     │      │        │
     └──────┴────────┘
            │
            ▼
 Quickshell.execDetached
            │
            ▼
 systemctl / loginctl
            │
            ▼
  system / session
```

There are effectively two responsibilities:

```text
Power
    maps intent to a command

systemd / logind
    executes the power or session change
```

Power should not duplicate the policy already provided by systemd and logind.

***

## 6.2 Command execution

All public actions funnel through one helper:

```text
shutdown / reboot / suspend / hibernate / lock / logout
                        │
                        ▼
                    _run(command)
                        │
                        ▼
              Quickshell.execDetached
```

`_run()` is a guard plus a launch:

```text
command missing or empty -> return false
otherwise                 -> execDetached + return true
```

Because every public action passes a hardcoded non-empty array, they normally return `true`. The `false` path only matters for `logout()` with a missing session, which returns before reaching `_run()`, and for direct `_run()` misuse.

***

## 6.3 Logout guard

Logout is the only action with a precondition:

```text
sessionId = XDG_SESSION_ID or ""

sessionId empty?
    yes -> warn "[Power] XDG_SESSION_ID is unavailable"
           return false
    no  -> _run(["loginctl", "terminate-session", sessionId])
           return true
```

The session id is read once as a reactive property:

```qml
readonly property string sessionId:
    String(
        Quickshell.env(
            "XDG_SESSION_ID"
        ) || ""
    )
```

Callers can therefore disable logout UI with:

```qml
Power.sessionId !== ""
```

instead of handling the `false` return after the fact.

***

## 6.4 IPC architecture

IPC is a thin external interface over the same service functions.

Conceptually:

```text
terminal
   │
   ▼
n0ctos-power
   │
   ▼
Power.qml
   │
   ▼
systemctl / loginctl
```

For example:

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-power shutdown
```

becomes conceptually:

```qml
Power.shutdown()
```

and:

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-power logout
```

becomes conceptually:

```qml
Power.logout()
```

The IPC layer returns the same `bool` the QML function returns.

***

## 6.5 Final architecture summary

The entire system can be viewed as:

```text
                         Component
                            │
                            │ function call
                            ▼
                    ┌─────────────────┐
                    │      Power      │
                    │                 │
                    │ sessionId/user  │
                    │ power actions   │
                    │ session actions │
                    │ _run() helper   │
                    └────────┬────────┘
                             │
                             │ execDetached
                             ▼
                    ┌─────────────────┐
                    │ systemd/logind  │
                    │                 │
                    │ systemctl       │
                    │ loginctl        │
                    └────────┬────────┘
                             │
                             ▼
                       system / session
```

The core rule is:

> **Components request what power action they need; `Power.qml` decides which `systemctl` / `loginctl` command runs it; the system handles how the action is executed.**


# Screens Service



`Screens.qml` is N0ctOS's centralized screen tracking and primary-screen service.

It gives every shell component one consistent place to read the remembered screen order, the live Quickshell screens, the connected names, and the resolved primary screen without touching `Config` or `Quickshell.screens` directly.

The service supports remembered priority order, live screen indexing, primary resolution, new-screen discovery, primary reassignment, Config persistence, and a mostly read-only IPC interface with two control operations.

The normal usage pattern is:

```text
Component
    │
    ▼
Screens
    │
    ├── remembered order
    ├── live screens
    └── resolved primary
    │
    ├──────┼────────┐
    ▼      ▼        ▼
 Config Quickshell Config
           │       homeConfig
           ▼
    system screens
```

***

# 1. What does it do?

`Screens.qml` remembers screen priority and resolves which connected screen is primary.

A component can read a simple value:

```qml
Screens.primaryScreenName
```

or a simple count:

```qml
Screens.count
```

or the full live object:

```qml
Screens.primaryScreen
```

The remembered order is persisted as a plain string array:

```json
{
    "screens": [
        "DP-1",
        "HDMI-A-1"
    ]
}
```

Disconnected screens intentionally stay in that array so their priority is preserved when they are reconnected later.

The effective primary is resolved in this order:

```text
remembered names in order
    ↓
first currently connected
    ↓
first live screen (fallback)
```

So a component can simply do:

```qml
Text {
    text:
        Screens.primaryScreenName
}
```

and not care where the value came from.

If no screen is connected, the service returns safe fallbacks (`null`, `""`, `0`, `[]`) instead of failing.

***

# 2. UI API

Import normally:

```qml
import QtQuick
import Quickshell

import qs.services
```

## Core API

| How to read                 | What does it do                                                                 |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Screens.isReady`           | `Config.isReady`. `false` until configuration is loaded.                        |
| `Screens.names`             | Remembered priority order, copy of `_screenNames`. Disconnected names are kept. |
| `Screens.screens`           | Live `Quickshell.screens` array of `ShellScreen` objects.                       |
| `Screens.connectedNames`    | Names of currently connected screens, copy of `_connectedNames`.                |
| `Screens.count`             | `Quickshell.screens.length`.                                                    |
| `Screens.primaryScreen`     | Resolved primary `ShellScreen`, or `null`. Always selected from live screens.   |
| `Screens.primaryScreenName` | `String(primaryScreen.name \|\| "")`, or `""` when none.                        |

## Functions and signals

| How to call                      | What does it do                                                                                                                                                        |
| -------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Screens.syncFromConfig()`       | Reloads `_screenNames` from `Config.get("screens", [])` with normalization. Returns `true` when the order changed, `false` otherwise.                                  |
| `Screens.saveNames(names)`       | Writes `names.slice()` to `Config.set("screens", ...)`. Returns `false` when not ready, otherwise the `Config.set()` result.                                           |
| `Screens.refresh()`              | Rebuilds the connected index, appends new screens to the remembered order, persists them, emits discovery signals, and re-resolves primary.                            |
| `Screens.resolvePrimary()`       | Re-resolves `primaryScreen` from remembered order plus live screens.                                                                                                   |
| `Screens.screenForName(name)`    | Returns the connected `ShellScreen` for `name`, or `null` when missing or empty.                                                                                       |
| `Screens.isConnected(name)`      | `true` when `screenForName(name)` is not `null`.                                                                                                                       |
| `Screens.setPrimary(name)`       | Moves a connected, remembered screen to the front of the order, persists it, and re-resolves primary. Returns `true` when it is primary afterwards, `false` otherwise. |
| `Screens.screenDiscovered(name)` | Signal emitted once per newly discovered screen, after public state is updated.                                                                                        |
| `Screens.configurationChanged()` | Signal emitted when the remembered order changes.                                                                                                                      |
| `Screens.refreshed()`            | Signal emitted at the end of every `refresh()`.                                                                                                                        |

### Typical component usage

```qml
Text {
    text:
        Screens.primaryScreenName
}

Text {
    text:
        Screens.count > 1
            ? Screens.count + " screens"
            : "single screen"
}

Repeater {
    model:
        Screens.screens

    delegate: Text {
        required property var modelData

        text:
            modelData.name
    }
}
```

That is the intended everyday usage.

Components normally should not need to know how remembered order, connected indexing, or `Config` persistence work.

***

# 3. IPC API

IPC target:

```text
n0ctos-screens
```

## Core reads

| How to call          | What does it do                                                                          |
| -------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `count`              | Returns `Screens.count` as an integer.                                                   |
| `primary`            | Returns `Screens.primaryScreenName` as a string.                                         |
| `names`              | Returns the remembered order as a JSON array string.                                     |
| `connected`          | Returns the connected names as a JSON array string.                                      |
| `isConnected <name>` | Returns `true` when the named screen is connected.                                       |
| `list`               | Returns one info object per live screen as a JSON array string.                          |
| `get <name>`         | Returns the info object for one connected screen as a JSON string, or `""` when unknown. |
| `getPrimary`         | Returns the info object for the primary screen as a JSON string, or `""` when none.      |

| Example                                       | Result                                                        |
| --------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `qs ipc call n0ctos-screens count`            | `2`                                                           |
| `qs ipc call n0ctos-screens primary`          | `"DP-1"`                                                      |
| `qs ipc call n0ctos-screens names`            | `["DP-1","HDMI-A-1"]`                                         |
| `qs ipc call n0ctos-screens connected`        | `["DP-1","HDMI-A-1"]`                                         |
| `qs ipc call n0ctos-screens isConnected DP-1` | `true`                                                        |
| `qs ipc call n0ctos-screens list`             | JSON array of screen info objects (see below)                 |
| `qs ipc call n0ctos-screens get DP-1`         | JSON info object for `DP-1` (see below), or `""` when unknown |
| `qs ipc call n0ctos-screens getPrimary`       | JSON info object for the primary screen, or `""` when none    |

For example:

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-screens count
```

returns:

```text
2
```

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-screens primary
```

returns:

```text
DP-1
```

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-screens names
```

returns:

```text
["DP-1","HDMI-A-1"]
```

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-screens isConnected DP-1
```

returns:

```text
true
```

`list` returns:

```json
[
    {
        "name": "DP-1",
        "model": "PA278QV",
        "serialNumber": "NCLM123456",
        "x": 0,
        "y": 0,
        "width": 2560,
        "height": 1440,
        "devicePixelRatio": 1,
        "logicalPixelDensity": 4.2,
        "physicalPixelDensity": 4.2
    },
    {
        "name": "HDMI-A-1",
        "model": "VP249",
        "serialNumber": "",
        "x": 2560,
        "y": 0,
        "width": 1920,
        "height": 1080,
        "devicePixelRatio": 1,
        "logicalPixelDensity": 3.8,
        "physicalPixelDensity": 3.8
    }
]
```

`get` returns one object with the same shape:

```json
{
    "name": "DP-1",
    "model": "PA278QV",
    "serialNumber": "NCLM123456",
    "x": 0,
    "y": 0,
    "width": 2560,
    "height": 1440,
    "devicePixelRatio": 1,
    "logicalPixelDensity": 4.2,
    "physicalPixelDensity": 4.2
}
```

When the name is unknown, `get` returns an empty string.

When no primary exists, `getPrimary` returns an empty string.

## Control operations

| How to call         | What does it do                                                                                                                             |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `setPrimary <name>` | Moves a connected, remembered screen to the front and re-resolves primary. Returns `true` when it is primary afterwards, `false` otherwise. |
| `refresh`           | Re-runs `Screens.refresh()`. Returns nothing.                                                                                               |

| Example                                          | Result                                                                     |
| ------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `qs ipc call n0ctos-screens setPrimary HDMI-A-1` | `true` when `HDMI-A-1` is connected and becomes primary, `false` otherwise |
| `qs ipc call n0ctos-screens refresh`             | no output                                                                  |

For example:

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-screens setPrimary HDMI-A-1
```

returns:

```text
true
```

when `HDMI-A-1` is connected, and:

```text
false
```

when the name is empty, not connected, or not in the remembered order.

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-screens refresh
```

produces no output. It only rebuilds the index and re-resolves primary.

***

# 4. Features / limitations

## Features

### Remembered priority order

The service keeps:

```text
_screenNames
```

as the priority list. It is loaded from:

```json
{
    "screens": [
        "DP-1",
        "HDMI-A-1"
    ]
}
```

and returned as:

```qml
Screens.names
```

Disconnected names are intentionally kept so reconnecting a monitor restores its position.

### Live screens stay live

Live objects always come from:

```text
Quickshell.screens
```

and are exposed directly as:

```qml
Screens.screens
```

The service never caches or clones `ShellScreen` objects. `primaryScreen` is always one of the current live objects.

### Primary resolution

`resolvePrimary()` walks the remembered order and picks the first currently connected screen:

```text
_screenNames[0] -> connected? -> primary
_screenNames[1] -> connected? -> primary
...
none connected -> Quickshell.screens[0]
none live      -> null
```

`primaryScreenName` is then:

```text
primaryScreen ? String(primaryScreen.name || "") : ""
```

### Automatic discovery

`refresh()` appends unknown connected names to the remembered order:

```text
connected not in _screenNames
    ↓
append to order
    ↓
saveNames()
    ↓
configurationChanged()
    ↓
screenDiscovered(name) per screen
```

The discovery signal fires only after public state is updated, so handlers can safely read `Screens.names` and `Screens.screens`.

### Config integration

The service does not implement its own JSON persistence.

Screen order is stored in:

```text
homeConfig
```

under the `screens` key through:

```qml
Config.get("screens", [])
Config.set("screens", names.slice())
```

`Config` already handles document state, watching, saving, and external reloads.

### No polling

The service does not repeatedly query screens on a timer.

It reacts to:

```text
Quickshell.onScreensChanged -> refresh()
Config.onExternalReload    -> syncFromConfig() + refresh()
Config.onRevisionChanged   -> syncFromConfig() + resolvePrimary()
Component.onCompleted      -> syncFromConfig() + refresh()
ready changes              -> syncFromConfig() + refresh()
```

***

## Limitations

### Names are connector strings

Screens are identified by connector names such as:

```text
DP-1
HDMI-A-1
eDP-1
```

There is no stable serial-based identity or user-visible label. Renaming a connector at the compositor level looks like a new screen.

### Primary is always a live screen

`primaryScreen` is never a disconnected object. If the remembered first screen is unplugged, primary moves to the next connected screen or to `Quickshell.screens[0]`.

A component must handle:

```qml
Screens.primaryScreen === null
```

and:

```qml
Screens.primaryScreenName === ""
```

on a system with no live screens.

### `setPrimary` is constrained

`setPrimary(name)` returns `false` when:

```text
name is empty
name is not connected
name is not in the remembered order
```

It does not add unknown names. The screen must already be discovered through `refresh()`.

### No per-screen settings

The service only stores order:

```json
{
    "screens": [
        "DP-1",
        "HDMI-A-1"
    ]
}
```

It does not store per-screen brightness, scale, position, wallpaper, or panel placement. Geometry comes from the live `ShellScreen` object, not from `Config`.

### Gated on `Config.isReady`

`syncFromConfig()`, `saveNames()`, and `refresh()` all return early when `Config.isReady` is `false`. Early `Quickshell.screens` changes before config load do not create persisted order until `isReady` fires.

***

# 5. Example use cases

## 5.1 A bar showing the primary screen

A bar only needs two bindings:

```qml
import QtQuick
import Quickshell

import qs.services

Row {
    spacing: 6

    Text {
        text:
            Screens.primaryScreenName
    }

    Text {
        text:
            Screens.count > 1
                ? Screens.count + " screens"
                : "single screen"
    }
}
```

The component does not need to know whether the primary came from:

```text
the first remembered screen
a fallback live screen
a recent setPrimary() call
a reconnection
```

It only receives the effective value.

***

## 5.2 One panel instance per screen

Live screens can drive per-screen windows directly:

```qml
import QtQuick
import Quickshell

import qs.services

Repeater {
    model:
        Screens.screens

    delegate: PanelWindow {
        required property var modelData

        screen:
            modelData

        Text {
            anchors.centerIn:
                parent

            text:
                modelData.name +
                (modelData.name === Screens.primaryScreenName
                    ? " (primary)"
                    : "")
        }
    }
}
```

When a monitor is plugged in or removed, `Quickshell.screens` changes, `refresh()` runs, and the repeater updates.

***

## 5.3 Reacting to new screens

Discovery is explicit:

```qml
import QtQuick

import qs.services

Connections {
    target:
        Screens

    function onScreenDiscovered(name) {
        console.info(
            "new screen:",
            name,
            Screens.isConnected(name)
        )
    }

    function onConfigurationChanged() {
        console.info(
            JSON.stringify(
                Screens.names
            )
        )
    }
}
```

`screenDiscovered` fires once per new name. `configurationChanged` fires whenever the remembered order array itself changes.

***

## 5.4 A primary-screen switcher

`setPrimary()` only reorders, so the UI is a simple list:

```qml
import QtQuick

import qs.services

Column {
    spacing: 8

    Repeater {
        model:
            Screens.connectedNames

        delegate: Rectangle {
            required property string modelData

            width: 180
            height: 34

            radius: 8

            color:
                Screens.primaryScreenName ===
                    modelData
                    ? "#2acfff"
                    : "#141d26"

            Text {
                anchors.centerIn:
                    parent

                text:
                    parent.modelData

                color:
                    Screens.primaryScreenName ===
                        parent.modelData
                        ? "#061018"
                        : "#ffffff"
            }

            MouseArea {
                anchors.fill:
                    parent

                onClicked:
                    Screens.setPrimary(
                        parent.modelData
                    )
            }
        }
    }
}
```

`setPrimary()` returns:

```text
true  -> the clicked screen is now primary
false -> it was not connected or not remembered
```

***

## 5.5 Terminal workflow

Read how many screens exist:

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-screens count
```

Read the primary name:

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-screens primary
```

Read the remembered order:

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-screens names
```

Read only connected names:

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-screens connected
```

Check one screen:

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-screens isConnected DP-1
```

Inspect every live screen:

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-screens list
```

Inspect one screen:

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-screens get DP-1
```

Inspect the primary screen:

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-screens getPrimary
```

Change the primary:

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-screens setPrimary HDMI-A-1
```

Force a re-scan:

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-screens refresh
```

***

# 6. Detailed architecture

This section is for developers working on `Screens.qml` and the services/components that consume it.

***

## 6.1 Overall architecture

The service is an index and priority layer between `Quickshell.screens` and `Config`.

```text
N0ctOS Component / Service
            │
            ▼
      Screens.qml
            │
     ┌──────┼────────┐
     │      │        │
     ▼      ▼        ▼
 remembered live   primary
  order   screens  resolution
     │      │        │
     └──────┴────────┘
            │
     ┌──────┴──────┐
     ▼             ▼
   Config      Quickshell
     │          screens
     ▼
 homeConfig
```

There are effectively two responsibilities:

```text
Screens
    screen identity, order, and primary selection

Config + Quickshell
    persistence and hardware detection
```

Screens should not duplicate the file management already provided by Config, or the topology detection already provided by Quickshell.

***

## 6.2 Remembered vs connected vs live

Three related but different lists exist:

```text
names
    remembered priority, includes disconnected
    _screenNames.slice()

connectedNames
    currently connected names only
    _connectedNames.slice()

screens
    live ShellScreen objects
    Quickshell.screens
```

The rule is:

```text
order     -> names
presence  -> connectedNames
objects   -> screens
selection -> primaryScreen
```

`screenForName()` bridges names and objects through the internal `_connectedByName` map.

***

## 6.3 Configuration structure

The service owns the `screens` key of `homeConfig`.

The structure is:

```json
{
    "screens": [
        "DP-1",
        "HDMI-A-1"
    ]
}
```

A single-monitor system might look like:

```json
{
    "screens": [
        "eDP-1"
    ]
}
```

The service itself does not require every name to be currently connected. Disconnected entries are valid data.

***

## 6.4 Normalization

`syncFromConfig()` normalizes the stored array:

```text
Config.get("screens", [])
    ↓
skip null / undefined
    ↓
String(value)
    ↓
skip "" and duplicates
    ↓
normalized array
```

It then compares element by element against `_screenNames`. If nothing changed it returns `false` without emitting `configurationChanged()`. Otherwise it replaces `_screenNames`, emits the signal, and returns `true`.

***

## 6.5 Refresh lifecycle

`refresh()` is the single topology ingest:

```text
guard Config.isReady and _refreshing
        │
        ▼
index Quickshell.screens by String(screen.name)
        │
        ▼
_connectedByName = prototype-less map
_connectedNames = connectedNames
        │
        ▼
new names? ── yes ──► append, saveNames(),
                       configurationChanged(),
                       screenDiscovered(name) per name
              │
              no
              │
              ▼
resolvePrimary()
        │
        ▼
_refreshing = false
        │
        ▼
refreshed()
```

The map uses `Object.create(null)` because connector names are arbitrary strings and must not collide with `Object.prototype` keys.

The `_refreshing` flag prevents reentrant refreshes when `saveNames()` triggers `onRevisionChanged()` mid-refresh.

***

## 6.6 Primary resolution

`resolvePrimary()` performs:

```text
walk _screenNames in order
    ↓
first name present in _connectedByName wins
    ↓
none matched + live screens exist -> Quickshell.screens[0]
    ↓
none live -> null
```

It then logs only when the name actually changed:

```text
[Screens] primary: DP-1
[Screens] primary: (none)
```

`setPrimary()` reuses this by moving the target to index `0` first:

```text
setPrimary("HDMI-A-1")
    │
    ▼
["DP-1","HDMI-A-1"] -> ["HDMI-A-1","DP-1"]
    │
    ▼
saveNames() + configurationChanged()
    │
    ▼
resolvePrimary()
    │
    ▼
primaryScreenName === "HDMI-A-1" ?
```

***

## 6.7 Config reactivity

External and local config changes take different paths on purpose:

```text
editor changes config file
        │
        ▼
Config.onExternalReload
        │
        ▼
syncFromConfig() + refresh()
```

because physical topology may also have changed, while:

```text
local Config.set("screens", ...)
        │
        ▼
Config.onRevisionChanged
        │
        ▼
syncFromConfig() + resolvePrimary()
```

because a revision bump alone does not mean new hardware appeared. Only primary selection needs updating.

Startup covers both cold paths:

```text
Component.onCompleted -> syncFromConfig() + refresh()
ready changes to true -> syncFromConfig() + refresh()
```

***

## 6.8 IPC architecture

IPC is a thin external interface over the same service state.

Conceptually:

```text
terminal
   │
   ▼
n0ctos-screens
   │
   ▼
Screens.qml
   │
   ├────▼────┐
   ▼         ▼
 Config   Quickshell
```

For example:

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-screens primary
```

becomes conceptually:

```qml
Screens.primaryScreenName
```

and:

```bash
qs ipc call n0ctos-screens get DP-1
```

becomes conceptually:

```qml
JSON.stringify(
    Screens._screenInfo(
        Screens.screenForName("DP-1")
    )
)
```

The IPC layer serializes screen objects as JSON strings for terminal use because raw `ShellScreen` objects cannot cross IPC.

***

## 6.9 Final architecture summary

The entire system can be viewed as:

```text
                          Component
                             │
                             │ property binding / function call
                             ▼
                     ┌─────────────────┐
                     │     Screens     │
                     │                 │
                     │ remembered order│
                     │ live index      │
                     │ primary         │
                     │ discovery       │
                     └────────┬────────┘
                              │
                              │ Config API + Quickshell API
                              ▼
                     ┌─────────────────┐
                     │ Config +        │
                     │ Quickshell      │
                     │                 │
                     │ homeConfig      │
                     │ screens         │
                     │ topology        │
                     └────────┬────────┘
                              │
                              ▼
                      config file + hardware
```

The core rule is:

> **Components read what screen state they need; `Screens.qml` decides remembered order and which connected screen is primary; `Config` handles how order is persisted and `Quickshell` handles how hardware topology is detected.**


# ServiceHost Infrastructure



`ServiceHost.qml` is N0ctOS's tiny startup helper that forces eager service creation.

It gives the shell entry point one place to touch singletons that must exist immediately instead of on first use.

Services listed in `eagerServices` are created at launch. Services not listed stay naturally lazy.

The normal usage pattern is:

```text
Shell entry point
    │
    ▼
ServiceHost
    │
    ├── eagerServices -> singleton instances created now
    └── all other services -> created on first use
```

***

# 1. What does it do?

`ServiceHost.qml` exists exactly once, created from the shell entry point.

It declares one property:

```qml
property list<QtObject> eagerServices: [
    ConfigStore,
    Config,
    DateTime,
    Screens,
    Clipboard,
    Power,
    Audio,
    Battery,
    Brightness,
    Network,
    Bluetooth,
    Media,
    Notifications,
    SystemTray,
    Animations,
    SoundFX
]
```

Referencing those singletons inside the list literal touches them, so their instances are created immediately at startup.

Any service not in that list is never touched here and remains lazily instantiated when first referenced elsewhere.

On completion it logs two lines:

```text
[N0ctOS Services] ServiceHost started
[N0ctOS Services] Eager services: 16
```

where `16` is the current `eagerServices.length`.

***

# 2. UI API

`ServiceHost` is not imported by components. It is instantiated once at startup. Components use the individual services directly.

## Core API

| How to read                   | What does it do                                                           |
| ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<host>.eagerServices`        | Ordered list of singleton instances to create eagerly at startup.         |
| `<host>.eagerServices.length` | Number of eager services (currently `16`). Used only for the startup log. |

### Typical instantiation

The shell entry point creates one host:

```qml
ServiceHost {
}
```

No per-component import or per-component setup is needed. Once the host exists, the listed singletons exist too.

That is the intended everyday usage.

Components normally should not need to reference `ServiceHost` at all.

***

# 3. IPC API

`ServiceHost.qml` defines no IPC target, so there is no IPC API.

***

# 4. Features / limitations

## Features

### One place for eager startup

All eagerly-started services are visible in a single 16-entry list, in declaration order.

### Lazy by default

A service gains eager startup only by being added to the list. Everything else keeps Quickshell's natural lazy behavior with no extra code.

### Startup logging

`Component.onCompleted` emits two `console.info` lines confirming the host started and how many services were marked eager.

### No persistence or polling

The file holds no configuration, watches no files, and runs no timers. It only references singletons and logs.

***

## Limitations

### Eager set is static

Adding or removing an eager service requires editing `eagerServices` in `ServiceHost.qml`. There is no runtime call to register or unregister a service.

### Log-only observability

The host reports only the eager count. It does not check readiness, health, or load order, and exposes no ready signal.

### Entry-point owned

The "exactly once" guarantee comes from the entry point creating one instance. The file itself does not enforce singleton construction.

***

# 5. Example use cases

## 5.1 Start all core services at launch

Create the host once from the shell entry point:

```qml
ServiceHost {
}
```

`ConfigStore`, `Config`, `DateTime`, and the remaining listed singletons are then alive before any panel or widget binds to them.

***

## 5.2 Confirm eager startup in logs

After launch, expect:

```text
[N0ctOS Services] ServiceHost started
[N0ctOS Services] Eager services: 16
```

A missing first line means the host was never instantiated. A wrong count means the list was edited.

***

## 5.3 Make a service eager

Add its singleton to the list:

```qml
property list<QtObject> eagerServices: [
    ConfigStore,
    Config,
    // ...
    Animations,
    SoundFX,
    MyNewService
]
```

Remove an entry to return that service to lazy creation.

***

# 6. Detailed architecture

This section is for developers working on `ServiceHost.qml` and shell startup.

***

## 6.1 Overall architecture

The host is a thin reference holder between the entry point and the service singletons:

```text
Shell entry point
        │
        ▼
  ServiceHost.qml (QtObject, id: root)
        │
        ▼
  eagerServices: list<QtObject>
        │
        ├── ConfigStore, Config, DateTime, Screens
        ├── Clipboard, Power, Audio, Battery
        ├── Brightness, Network, Bluetooth, Media
        └── Notifications, SystemTray, Animations, SoundFX
```

There is one responsibility:

```text
ServiceHost
    touch listed singletons at startup + log count
```

It implements no service logic itself.

***

## 6.2 Eager vs lazy

The rule is:

```text
listed in eagerServices -> created when host is created
```
